# StateKit Full Porting Plan — exec & state, all platforms

Companion to `plans/init.md` (scope/DoD) and `plans/testing.md` (verification).
Goal: bring **every** SaltStack exec & state family from the pinned catalog
(`docs/catalog/`, revision `references/salt.lock`) to an explicit terminal
state — *ported*, or *excluded with a recorded reason* — including non-Linux
operating systems.

Baseline at plan creation:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Catalog families (exec+states) | 246 |
| Implemented | 34 |
| Functions implemented | 133 exec / 24 states (catalog totals: 4284 / 669) |
| Not applicable (auto-classified) | 69 families |
| Deferred | 143 families |

## 0. Principles

1. **Contract-first**: every ported function mirrors the pinned Salt source
   (`docs/catalog/<kind>/<module>.yaml`) — signature, return shape, comments;
   divergences recorded under `docs/compatibility/` per init.md §28.
2. **No blind ports**: a family enters a round only with its Salt unit-test
   references mapped to StateKit fixtures.
3. **Dependency policy**: no new Go module dependencies. External system
   binaries are called through the central Runner; stdlib implementations are
   preferred where they enable hermetic tests. Any exception requires an ADR.
4. **Per-family DoD** = init.md §47–48: contract tests green on every platform
   the family declares, fixtures present, compatibility annotation written.
5. Terminal states per family: `implemented` / `partial` (documented subset) /
   `excluded` (reason + ADR line: master-minion-by-design, platform-EOL,
   impossible without Go deps).

## 1. Enablers (must land before dependents)

| ID | Deliverable | Unblocks | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | **Runner v2 OS profiles**: per-GOOS/runtime shell model (`sh` / PowerShell 7 / cmd), argv escaping, binary suffix, env semantics | Windows, macOS tracks | profile unit tests; smoke on GH `windows-*`/`macos-*` runners |
| E2 | **Elevation model**: sudo/doas (unix), runas/UAC notes (windows) behind one `Elevate(ctx, cmd)`; non-root failure contracts preserved (init.md §39) | storage, firewall, package, service rounds | fake-runner units; privileged containers; QEMU |
| E3 | **Platform-scoped registration**: build-tag trees `modules/exec/<family>/os_{linux,darwin,windows,bsd,solaris}.go`; registry registers by runtime facts; `--list` becomes platform-aware | R6–R8 | cross-GOOS build matrix extended (windows/darwin/freebsd) |
| E4 | **Facts v2**: per-OS providers (win: registry/CIM via PowerShell; mac: `system_profiler`, `dscl`; bsd: `sysctl`/`kenv`) feeding PackageManager/InitSystem/Virt | platform rounds, pkg/service selection | golden facts fixtures per OS image |
| E5 | **Services test tier**: compose harness booting real mysql/postgres/redis/rabbitmq/mongo/elasticsearch/kafka | R9 | new `integration-services.yml` |
| E6 | **QEMU promotion**: vm-nightly becomes blocking for `vm-required` suites | R1, R2, R8 | Packer recipes in `tests/images/vm/` |
| E7 | **Compatibility ledger v2**: buckets renamed `implemented/partial/excluded/planned`; every family carries target round + ADR link | all rounds | existing golden determinism |


## 2. Rounds

Sizing = Salt functions in scope (catalog counts). Each round ends with
coverage regen, differential scope extension for its families, gates green.

### R1 — Linux storage & filesystem CLIs (~90 funcs)
`lvm`, `linux_lvm`, `partition`, `extfs`, `xfs`, `mdadm_raid`, `bcache`,
`devmap`, `loop`, `cryptdev`, `quota`, blockdev extensions, pkg_resource
helpers. Binaries: lvm toolset, parted/lsblk, mkfs.*, xfs tools, mdadm,
losetup, cryptsetup, quota.
Verify: hermetic argv tests + **QEMU** loopback-disk suites (E6); differential
vs Salt in privileged VM images.

### R2 — Linux network, firewall, hardware (~110 funcs)
`iptables`, `nftables`, `firewalld`, `ipset`, `ip`, `route`, `network`
(read-only /sys/class/net with `ip` fallback), `bridge`, `ethtool`, `sysfs`,
`udev`, `ps`, `process`, `scsi`, `smbios`, `devinfo`, `iwtools`,
`kernelpkg_linux_apt/_yum` (on the pkg provider).
Verify: argv units + QEMU; differential on normalized iptables/nftables dumps.

### R3 — Package ecosystem deepening (~70 funcs)
`pkgrepo` (apt/yum/zypper), `pkgbuild` (rpm/deb), `alternatives`,
`debconfmod`, `python`, `pyenv`, virtualenv/npm/pip long tail.
Verify: Tier 1 six-distro matrix; differential install/remove/list cycles of
throwaway packages per provider.

### R4 — Files, text, templates, misc Linux (~80 funcs)
`file.*` long tail (patch, blockreplace, makedirs_perms, copy options),
`cp` (local source), `incron`, logrotate extras, `temp`, `xml` (encoding/xml),
`yaml` (existing dep), and `jinja`: Salt-compatible
`jinja.import_yaml`, `jinja.import_json`, and `jinja.load_map` use a bounded
system/venv Python CLI bridge with Jinja2. StateKit also provides the opt-in,
non-Salt `gotemplate.render`, `gotemplate.import_yaml`,
`gotemplate.import_json`, and `gotemplate.load_map` functions on stdlib
`text/template`. `file.apply_template_on_contents` is registered, but supports
only `template=gotemplate`; `template=jinja` and other engines return the Salt
unsupported map. Full Salt renderer semantics, Salt custom import tags,
loader/pillar/grains, `file.get_managed` templated-source handling, and state
file templating remain deferred/excluded; this is an explicit compatibility
ceiling, not a claim of full Jinja parity. Also includes `data`, `defaults`,
`out`, `ret`, `restartcheck`, and the status long tail.
Verify: hermetic unit + fixture suites.

### R5 — Security, crypto, auth on Linux (~85 funcs)
`ssh_auth`, `ssh_known_hosts` (FS parsing first), `ssh_pki`, `x509`, `tls`,
`asymmetric`, `webutil`, `gpg`, `nacl`, `pam`, selinux booleans/modules
(semanage), `linux_acl`.
Binaries: openssl, ssh-keygen, gpg, getfacl/setfacl, semanage.
Verify: container suites; differential for authorized_keys and self-signed
x509 generation (normalized PEM).

### R6 — macOS track (~55 funcs)
`mac_user`(dscl), `mac_group`, mac pkg/brew, launchctl service variant,
`macdefaults`, `keychain`(security), `softwareupdate`, `desktop`, `assistive`,
`xattr`, `power`, `macpackage`.
Enablers: E1–E4. CI: `macos-*` runners; platform-split fixture roots;
darwin binaries already build in release matrix.
Verify: host-runner smoke; differential where Salt installs via pip.

### R7 — Windows track (~230 funcs, largest)
`reg`, `dism`, `dsc(_resource)`, `lgpo`, `lgpo_reg`, `win_firewall`,
`win_dns_client`, `win_iis`, `win_servermanager`, `win_path`, `win_pki`,
`win_dacl`, `win_event`, task(schtasks), `powercfg`, `rdp`, license,
autoruns, auditpol, wua, wusa, psget, chocolatey, winrepo, shortcut,
smtp_server, snmp-windows, appx, plus win_file/user/group/service/pkg/
timezone variants, certutil.
Enablers: E1–E4 mandatory; PowerShell scriptlets emitted by Runner profile;
registry access through `reg.exe` (no Go deps).
CI: `windows-*` runners; dedicated fixture root; differential where Salt is
installable.
Sequencing inside R7: core objects first (reg→user/group/service/pkg/file),
then policy stacks (lgpo/firewall/dns), then optional roles (iis/smtp/snmp).

### R8 — BSD / Solaris tracks (~60 funcs)
freebsd (`pkgng`, pw_user/pw_group), openbsd/netbsd small sets,
`solaris_system/user/group/shadow/fmadm/logadm/rbac/ipspkg/smf_service`,
`zoneadm`, `zonecfg`.
Enablers: E3/E4/E6. CI: QEMU cloud images (freebsd/openbsd/netbsd/solaris 11)
promoted to blocking after soak.
Verify: same fixture format; differential best-effort (Salt on BSD/Solaris is
install-constrained — record coverage caveats).

### R9 — Databases & brokers via native CLIs (~120 funcs)
`mysql`, `postgres*`(10 families), redis-cli, mongosh, influx, elasticsearch
(REST via http.query core), kafka, rabbitmqctl family, cassandra cqlsh,
couchbase, zk_concurrency. SQLite-backed execution uses the declared,
CGO-free `modernc.org/sqlite` database/sql driver rather than a sqlite3 CLI;
dependency provenance and quarantine verification remain pending. Enabler: E5.
Credentials passed per-fixture; secrets never logged (Runner redaction).
Verify: services tier integration + differential for list/create/drop cycles
on disposable databases.

### R10 — Cloud & SaaS APIs (~70 funcs)
Policy: vendor CLI wrappers first (`aws`, `az`, `gcloud`, `doctl`, `govc`),
thin stdlib HTTP for webhook-style APIs (slack_notify, telegram, twilio,
victorops, pagerduty, github/gitlab signatures — hmac core exists).
Families: cloud*, boto*/ec2/route53 subsets actually exercised by CLIs,
azurearm, google_*, gcp_*, digital_ocean, linode, vsphere/esxi/govc,
openstack stack (keystone/glance/heat/neutron/nova/cinder/swift),
dnsutil/dig (bind9-client), netbox, saltcloud.
Excluded-by-ADR candidates: any API requiring OAuth flows or signed request
canonicalization beyond stdlib scope.
Verify: contract tests against recorded-response fixtures; live smoke behind
opt-in label only.

### R11 — Network devices (plugin boundary) (~40 funcs)
`napalm_*`, `junos`, `nxos(_api)`, `arista_pyeapi`, netmiko-style drivers.
Requires SSH/NETCONF clients — either pure-Go SSH (stdlib has none → would
break dependency policy) or out-of-tree plugin consuming external CLIs.
Decision gate: ADR before R11 starts; default outcome = plugin boundary
documented, core repo ships discovery/error contracts only.

## 3. Cross-cutting workstreams

- **States mirror exec**: every exec round ships its state counterparts in the
  same round (DoD blocks otherwise).
- **Fixtures**: each family adds real-case scenarios under its suite directory
  (testing.md §"Real-case coverage families"); vm-required flags respected.
- **Differential**: scope grows one round behind ports (R_n ports → R_{n+1}
  differential), report artifacts retained 90 days.
- **Compatibility annotations**: `docs/compatibility/<family>.md` per init.md
  §28 classification checklist; ledger v2 links them.
- **Coverage targets** (of relevant-exec set): R2→20%, R5→30%, R7+R8→55%,
  R9+R10→75%, final terminal-state reconciliation → 100% of catalog.
- **Estimation**: ~700 functions remain across rounds; sequencing DAG:
  E1–E4 → {R1,R2,R3,R4,R5} parallelizable → {R6,R7,R8} after enablers →
  R9 after E5 → R10 anytime after R4 → R11 last (ADR-gated).

## 4. Risks & mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Windows/mac CI cost | path-filtered platform jobs; nightly full, PR fast lane |
| Flaky service-tier tests | compose healthchecks + retry-once annotation policy (testing.md §Cost controls) |
| Salt drift | catalog re-index job fails golden check on submodule bump |
| Protocol client creep into Go deps | ADR gate; wrapper-first default |
| Scope explosion in jinja/templating | bounded Python Jinja2 bridge and opt-in Go templates; full Salt renderer semantics remain deferred/excluded |

## 5. Acceptance

- [ ] Every catalog family appears in exactly one terminal bucket
      (implemented / partial / excluded) with annotations.
- [ ] Each round's suites green across declared platforms before DoD claims.
- [ ] Differential reports exist for every ported family with runtime parity
      potential.
- [ ] Zero new Go module dependencies at completion (ADR-listed exceptions).

hermetically by fake-Runner tests). exportdb dispatches the fixed
shell-free `udevadm info --export-db` exactly once (LC_ALL=C, 30s timeout,
16MiB/64KiB capture budgets), validates the strict `subsystems *[]string`
filter before any dispatch, and filters client-side after complete
parsing behind finite parser/filter ceilings that fail closed with no
partial results. Documented divergences from Salt: fixed value-free
errors instead of echoing udevadm stderr (errors.Is preserved only for
context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded/process.ErrOutputLimit); int64/float64
numeric coercion vs Python unbounded int; LF-only line splitting vs
splitlines; singleton E map kept vs upstream `_normalize_info` KeyError;
parser/filter ceilings absent upstream (compatibility/safety ceilings,
not fleet capacity guarantees). Trust note (SEC-03/CQ-7): the parent
Runner resolves the bare executable `udevadm` via the caller/deployment's
parent `PATH`; callers/deployments must ensure both that `PATH` and the
selected `udevadm` helper are trusted. The child `Env=[LC_ALL=C]` pins
locale only, not executable identity; no resolver/authenticator is added
by design. Output sensitivity (SEC-03): a successful exportdb
database enumerates hardware and device identifiers and properties
(DEVPATH, DEVNAME, symlinks, modalias, and similar) — the subsystems
filter narrows returned records but is not collection minimization or
authorization; do not indiscriminately log or publish exportdb results.
The filter ceilings are enforced twice: at input decode (per-field
maxentries/maxentrybytes/maxtotalbytes tag bounds checked before any
destination list is materialized, including a raw comma-value ceiling
that rejects delimiter-heavy inputs) and inside the module as an explicit
invariant for decoder-bypassing callers. GitHub CI result remains
pending_external_ci.
R2.1 closeout (udev.name/path/links, PTD-EXEC-1640/1641/1642): the last
three udev wrappers over info(dev) — returning devices[0]["N"]/"P"/"S"
or nil when the section is absent (.get(..., None)) — registered through
the same shell-free `udevadm info --export --query=all
--{name|path}={dev}` dispatch with info's existing error policy (Runner
error passthrough, stderr echo on nonzero exit, strict parseInfo error
propagation, "no device found for %s" on empty parse), completing the
udev family at 6/6 public; the regenerated R2 report reads 186 catalog /
125 public / 125 registered with empty pending_public and still no live
twin scenario (contracts pinned hermetically by fake-Runner tests). No
upstream unit tests exist for the three wrappers; behavior is pinned by
local mocks. GitHub CI result remains pending_external_ci.
Enablers E1-E4 are complete: R6-R8 unblocked. Known gap
parked for R8: statfs_unix.go (!windows tag) does not compile under
GOOS=openbsd/netbsd (pre-existing, outside gated matrix). loop.until is
excluded per docs/adr/0001-loop-until-excluded.md; until_no_eval waits
for the data/util layer. Remaining in R1, in order:
  1. blockdev "extensions": no catalog entry exists for blockdev.*
     (info was a pre-catalog extension); nothing to port without a
     differential catalog pass. With that, R1's function scope is
     exhausted — R1 closes after a differential-scope pass over its
     families (R1 ports → R2 differential per section 3).
  2. Round status: **R2 CLOSED** (ports + differential scope pass,
     report at docs/differential/R2/report.yaml). Next: R3 pkg deep
     port (head item); R4-R5 per plan; R6-R8 unblocked via E1-E4; R9
     awaits the services tier (E5); R10 cloud; R11 netdev behind the
     ADR gate. Twin-container differential runs activate with
     differential.yml.

R3.1 opened the package deepening round with the APT repository surface
(the pkgrepo family, exec side): the Debian sources engine ported from
salt/utils/pkg/deb.py — classic SourceEntry/SourcesList plus Deb822
section stanzas, cdrom-line parsing, first-bracket-group option
extraction, split_source_line's bracket-aware walk, repo_line rendering
with trusted=no dropping and comment round-trip — and seven
CLI-facing pkg.* functions registered from the new modules/exec/pkgrepo
package: list_repos with deb822 per-uri/suite/type expansion, get_repo
with ppa expansion and slash-insensitive matching, del_repo with
suite/comps subtraction, the two cleanup-message shapes and the
sources.list.d part-file removal, mod_repo with the full kwargs
machinery (consolidate dedup onto sources.list deleting every
processed part file, keyid/keyserver/key_url/key_text side doors,
.sources creation behind the signedby/trusted gate when apt-key is
absent, the _MODIFY_OK/_MODIFY_OK_LEGACY setattr allow-lists), plus
get_repo_keys/add_repo_key/del_repo_key over gpg --with-colons parsing
and the .asc armor-preservation rule from regression #68464. Upstream
quirks pinned by tests: del_repo formats LP_PVT_SRC_FORMAT with swapped
arguments (DIST before OWNER), _decrypt_key returns the .decrypted path
even when dearmoring failed, get_repo_keys references an undefined
local on apt-key failure (StateKit raises an explicit error instead),
and the SyntaxError guard around _split_repo_str is dead code at the
pinned revision because parse raises SaltInvocationError. Documented
divergences: remote schemes surface UnsupportedError for cp.cache_file
until the cp family lands while local absolute paths pass through,
systemd-run scoping is not reproduced though the dpkg-lock retry
backoff is, comps set-difference keeps first-seen order where Python's
set iteration is unordered, truncated gpg colon-records degrade missing
fields to None instead of crashing, and config.option degrades like
minions lacking the module so proxy env injection for apt-key calls
stays inert. Salt's test_aptpkg repo surface maps onto hermetic
MemoryFS/fake-runner fixtures; expandRepoDef is ported internally for
the pkgrepo state module (managed/absent), which lands as its own phase
and flips the family terminal (exec 379→386; catalog regen also
reconciled the stale implemented_families list that had drifted since
R2.5 — network/nftables now recorded, summary consistent at 57
implemented / 120 planned).

R3.2 completed the yum/dnf repository surface and unified the pkg.*
registrations behind Salt's virtual-module selection: backendOf routes
on OS family (Debian→apt engine, RedHat→yum engine; zypper stays
unsupported until its phase, and the apt-only key trio reports
unsupported on other families). The yum side ports configparser
semantics into a local subset — lowercased keys, first-occurring "=" /
":" delimiter, indented continuations joined with "\n", DEFAULT
sections invisible to iteration, strict duplicate detection,
MissingSectionHeaderError degrading _parse_repo_file to ("", {}) — plus
yum.conf reposdir discovery over the /etc/yum/yum.conf, /etc/yum.conf,
/etc/dnf/dnf.conf, /etc/tdnf/tdnf.conf lookup order with the verbatim
no-config error list. list/get/del/mod_repo carry the upstream message
shapes (including the copr alias expansion inside the not-found text),
the single-file deletion path, comment-preserving multi-stanza rewrites
with multiline value re-indentation, COPR name mapping
(copr:owner/name → copr:copr.fedorainfracloud.org:owner:name), and the
mod_repo kwargs machinery where every non-dunder kwarg lands in the
stanza (basedir included — upstream never filters it) while blank-value
deletion keeps False and numeric zero because Python evaluates
False == 0. Documented divergences: option apply order is sorted where
upstream preserves request insertion order (Go map decoding loses it),
and .repo file scans iterate deterministically where os.listdir is
arbitrary. Salt's test_yumpkg repo tests map onto hermetic fixtures;
the CLI dispatch was smoke-checked against a live Fedora repos.d.

R3.3 completed the zypper repository surface: a scoped port of the
_Zypper wrapper (argv assembly with --non-interactive/--xmlout/
--no-refresh-unless-refreshable/--root, the success 0/100-103 and
warning 6/7/106/107 exit-code classification, XML
<message type="error"> extraction over an encoding/xml DOM subset, and
the lock-7 retry loop with five-second waits behind an injectable hook)
plus list/get/del/mod_repo and refresh_db. The del_repo XML feedback
contract keeps upstream's fall-through not-found raise when `rr`
returns no progress/message nodes; mod_repo carries URL-parse
six-tuple equality for the duplicate-alias probe, remove-and-readd on
baseurl changes, the mr flag ordering (enabled/refresh/cache/gpgcheck/
priority/humanname/name), and the no-op comment marker; refresh_db
tolerates retcode 6 via success_retcodes and parses up-to-date/done
lines. Documented divergences: systemd-run scoping is not reproduced,
event.fire_master lock notifications are dropped (master-minion
excluded) while the wait-and-retry behavior remains, and the rpm-lock
fcntl probe is not reproduced (zypper-lock retries cover exit 7).
Salt's test_zypperpkg refresh_db argv shapes and the zypp/*.cfg repo
fixtures map onto hermetic fake-runner/MemoryFS tests.

R3.4 landed the pkgrepo state module (managed/absent) and flipped the
family terminal. managed ports the full flow — the key-argument
conflict battery, enabled/disabled inversion per family, the
already-configured comparison loop (comps/key_url set compares, the
Debian line comparison with sorted tails and comment text, RedHat
comment combining, boolean disambiguation for 1/0 vs True/False),
clean_file staleness reconfiguration (#68208), the test-mode delta, and
the mod_repo/post-get_repo change recording — delegating to the
registered pkg.* functions; ExpandRepoDef/SplitRepoStr are exported
from the exec package mirroring Salt's cross-module private imports.
absent carries ppa/copr renaming, deb strip_uri, the architecture-
mismatch invalidation, and optional key removal. The catalog
classifier fix ships alongside: classifyFamilies previously received
only exec-side shipped names, so state-led families could never reach
terminal; with both surfaces counted, pkgrepo flipped implemented and
the same gap surfaced a second latent family — host — whose state
module predates the porting plan but lacked only() against its catalog.
host.only plus the hosts.get_alias/set_host exec long tail were ported
in this phase to complete it honestly (exec 386→388, states 32→35,
families 57→59 implemented / 118 planned).

R3.5 landed the pkgbuild exec surface behind backend dispatch:
pkgbuild.make_src_pkg/build/make_repo route rpm (rpmbuild/mock/
createrepo) on RedHat/SUSE families and deb (pbuilder/debuild/reprepro)
on Debian hosts, mirroring both backends' __virtual__ guards. String
commands run through a shlex-equivalent splitter matching Salt's
python_shell=False handling, preserving the quoted --define pairs
(rpm "_topdir"/"dist .el6"), the mock init/install/build cycle with
--no-clean accumulation across SRPMs, the deb salt-tarball rename dance
(- to _ plus "+ds", tar repack ending in `debuild -S -uc -us -sa`), the
.dsc passthrough branch, pbuilder create/update/build sequencing, and
reprepro includedsc/includedeb flows including the last-deb result
retention quirk. Documented boundaries: cp.get_url accepts readable
local absolute paths only (remote/salt schemes UnsupportedError),
keyid signing is pillar-gated — StateKit reproduces upstream's
format-string behavior where absent pillar names render as <gnupghome>/
None and the gpg delegate absence maps onto the verbatim re-raised
import error — and the salt.utils.vt interactive passphrase loops are
unported (unreachable without pillar); runas stays single-user.
Upstream ships integration-only tests for this family, so hermetic
tests pin argv sequences, env-helper batteries (including the dead
mandatory back-fill leaving codename empty when CODENAME is absent
from a provided env), and error texts directly. Family flipped
terminal under the classifier's prefix rule with the state module's
built/repo still owed — flagged for the R3 close differential pass
(exec 388→391, families 59→60 implemented / 117 planned).

R3.6 landed the alternatives family (9 CLI-facing functions including
the __func_alias__ set_→set registration): per-family command selection
(alternatives on RedHat, update-alternatives elsewhere), the shared
stderr-on-failure return shape for display/install/remove/auto/set, the
three-way show_link strategy (direct metadata-file second-line read on
RedHat/SUSE with family-specific directories, --query Link: parsing on
Debian), and readlink-based show_current/check_installed. Mapped onto
the full pytests battery including the Debian query fixture and both
metadata-file variants (exec 391→400, families 60→61 implemented /
116 planned).

R3.7 landed the debconf family across both surfaces. The exec module
(debconf.get_selections/show/set/set_template/set_file with the set_
alias) ports the (?ms) record regex unpacking, the fetchempty grouping,
and the temp-file set flow whose line format is pinned through runner
capture; both __virtual__ guards (Debian family plus the
debconf-utils presence probe) run per call with verbatim messages.
set_template stays UnsupportedError pending templating scoping and
set_file's salt:// scheme surfaces the cp.cache_file boundary like the
pkg families. The state module ports set_file (context/defaults dict
validation texts, test-mode comment, success/failure comments) and set
(the unchanged-answers accumulation, lowercase boolean serialization
before str(), password hiding, per-question failure marking), iterating
questions in sorted order where Python preserves request order
(documented divergence). Mapped onto both upstream pytest batteries
(exec 400→405, states 35→37; debconf family flips terminal, families
61→62 implemented / 115 planned).

R3.8 landed the python and pyenv families. python.run/script execute
snippets through a pinned interpreter: upstream targets sys.executable
(the minion's bundled interpreter) while StateKit resolves python3 from
PATH behind an injectable hook (documented divergence — no bundled
runtime). run keeps the shlex arg handling, the "Must specify either
'command' or 'args'" gate, rstrip, and the success_retcodes/stdout/
stderr overrides; script keeps the cache-error result shape
({pid:0, retcode:1, stdout:"", stderr:"", cache_error:true}), the
extension-preserving temp script in cwd with post-run cleanup, and the
salt:// scheme boundary via cp.cache_file UnsupportedError. pyenv ports
the PYENV_ROOT-prefixed exec wrapper with its is_installed gate,
config.option-driven root resolution (/usr/local/pyenv or ~user/.pyenv),
install/update/uninstall_python lifecycle (BSD MAKE=gmake and
pyenv.build_env env composition), versions/default/list/rehash, and the
do/do_with_python shim execution — `cd X && git pull` compounds run as
git -C equivalents and do()'s shell PATH expansion happens in-process
(both documented). The state module mirrors installed/absent/
install_pyenv including the pinned user-as-python quirk in install_pyenv;
Salt's non-standard result "default" key maps into StateResult.Meta.Extra.
Mapped onto both pytests batteries (exec 405→418, states 37→40; python
and pyenv families flip terminal, families 62→64 implemented / 113
planned).

R3.9 landed the pkgbuild state module: built (the results-requirement
gate, sorted missing-artifact verification against dest_dir, force/test
comments, and the build→re-verify cycle with the exec-side change dict)
and repo (test-mode refresh comment, retcode-driven result, refresh
change key, and the stdout/stderr comment concatenation). Upstream
ships integration-only tests, so hermetic tests pin the state flows
end-to-end through a scripted fake toolchain. The upstream fallback
indirection (rpmbuild.build/rpmbuild.make_repo names on non-RPM
families) collapses into the family-dispatched pkgbuild.* surface
(documented divergence); repo()'s invalid-env initialization quirk
(result staying True with only a comment) is preserved verbatim
(states 40→42; pkgbuild's owed state surface is now complete).

Long-tail audit for R3 close: npm misses cache_path/cache_list/

R3.10 completed the npm family with the cache trio
(cache_path/cache_list/cache_clean): upstream argv sequences including

R3.11 replaced the reduced pre-plan virtualenv.create with the full
contract and completed the family: create ports both toolchain branches
(venv via the interpreter hook, virtualenv with the version-window
flag logic for distribute/never_download/--download), all six venv-only
and virtualenv-only option guards with verbatim texts, the quoted
--prompt token, and the run_all-dict failure return (no error on nonzero
retcode). The pip/setuptools bootstrap scripts hit the cp.cache_file
boundary — https URLs surface UnsupportedError, so create(pip=True)
only completes where pip already exists (documented boundary).
virtualenv_ver parses the version-looking tokens, strips rc/+ds suffixes,
and renders the verbatim failure text including Python-style argv/dict
reprs. get_site_packages/get_distribution_path/get_resource_path/
get_resource_content embed the upstream Python source strings verbatim
(pkg_resources vs importlib.metadata split included) behind the
safe_py_code guard and the bin/python verification error. Exec 421→426;

R3.12 completed the pip family, replacing the reduced pre-plan surface
with the full contract across eleven CLI-facing functions. install
ports the complete kwargs machinery: version-gated legacy flags
(use_wheel/no_use_wheel/no_binary), the log file validation chain,
proxy composition with the global-config fallback, the timeout
float/int validation text, index/mirror validation with the pip>=7
mirrors rejection, exists_action s/i/w/b validation, VENV_PIP_TARGET
inheritance, the semicolon-to-comma pkgs quirk, the editable #egg
guard, extra_args dict/positional handling, VIRTUAL_ENV injection for
directory bin_env values, and the pip 10+ short-circuit returning
{"retcode": 0, "stdout": "No packages to install."} after exactly one
version probe. uninstall carries the requirements-dedup quirk; freeze
pins the --all floor and the #68214 --disable-pip-version-check
placements; list_/list_freeze_parse cover the JSON and freeze-parse
paths including -e/#egg and === records; list_upgrades keeps all three
output-format branches; upgrade() diffs the before/after lists
symmetrically. Binary resolution mirrors the ranked venv search
(python < python3 < pythonX.Y) with upstream's os.access semantics —
nonexistent paths yield the Access-denied message. Divergences
documented in-package: no bundled salt-pip branch (PATH interpreter
hook), no user-scoped requirements tempdir copying (single-user model),
salt:// requirements surfacing cp.cache_file UnsupportedError.
Exec 426→434.

R3 CLOSED. The differential scope pass (docs/differential/R3/report.yaml,
generated by tests/differential TestR3DifferentialReport with the
stale-report CI gate) reconciles the registry against the catalog for
the twelve scope files: every R3-listed family is fully covered —
alternatives 9/9, debconf 5/5, pkgbuild 3+3 (deb/rpm backends),
npm 6/6, pip 12/12, pyenv 11/11, python 2/2 (+2 state functions),
virtualenv 6/6 — and the provider repo surfaces register under pkg.*
like upstream's loader (aptpkg 13/34 public, yumpkg 10/39,
zypperpkg 10/42). The pending lists record the pkg provider long tail
(install/upgrade machinery, locks, groups, file_dict/list) which was
never in R3 scope; it belongs to a dedicated package-provider round
alongside the Tier 1 six-distro differential matrix from testing.md.
Round totals across scope files: 261 catalog functions, 172 public,
90 registered, plus the pkgrepo state module and four new state
families (pkgrepo/debconf/pyenv/pkgbuild + python states).

R4.1 opened the files round with the first file.* long-tail slice (22
functions registered via file.RegisterExt): path utilities
(basename/dirname/normpath/pardir/join with absolute-component reset and
path_exists_glob over the FS), text edits (prepend with the verbatim
"Prepended N lines" reply, seek_read/seek_write with in-place overwrite
semantics, truncate, and the comment/comment_line/uncomment trio whose
Python $ anchoring before a trailing newline is reproduced by matching
newline-stripped lines — including upstream's lstrip quirk where
uncommenting "# pcspkr" leaves the leading space), blockreplace with
the full marker machinery (auto linesep detection, append_newline None
semantics, append/prepend/insert_before/insert_after not-found
branches, dry_run, .bak backup, unified diff or boolean by show_changes,
and the unterminated-block error), directory ops (makedirs_ walk-up
messages, makedirs_perms, readdir with . / .. prefix, rmdir with
recurse/verbose), and links (link/is_hardlink via st_nlink behind
build-tagged syscall access, is_link, symlink with idempotent-target,
force-replace, and the absolute-path guard).

The FileSystem abstraction gained Link and Glob (OS + memory backends;
the memory hard link copies content — divergence documented). Exec
434→456.

R4.2 added the checksum/ownership/device slice (22 functions via
RegisterSums and RegisterDevices). Checksums: get_sum (missing files
return the literal "File not found" string — verbatim), get_hash with
chunked reads, check_hash with the ":"/"=" separators, the
length-to-type revmap and the verbatim supported-types enumeration
error; extract_hash ports the line-scanning machinery with the
source_hash_name > file_name > source priority, the partial first-hash
fallback, and the lookaround-free hex-boundary emulation (RE2 has no
lookbehind). Ownership: user_to_uid/uid_to_user/group_to_gid/gid_to_group
over os/user with upstream fallback semantics (missing names yield ""),
get_uid/get_user/get_gid/get_group degrading to -1/false like stats
defaults. lstat returns the st_* attribute dict (empty on error);
access implements f/r/w/x with the verbatim guards. Device nodes probe
and create against the real OS filesystem (memory nodes cannot carry
device metadata — documented): is_chrdev/is_blkdev/is_fifo/get_devmm
plus mknod_chrdev/mknod_blkdev/mknod_fifo/mknod with EEXIST comment
paths; mknod dev-number signatures split per GOOS behind thin adapters.
Exec 456→478.

R4.3 landed seven families (39 functions). cp covers the local-source
subset (cache_file/cache_local_file/is_cached/get_file/get_url/
get_file_str/hash_file): file:// and bare local paths copy through the
FS with dest-directory handling and MkdirAll; salt:// stays permanently
excluded, remote schemes surface UnsupportedError until a fetcher lands,
and the master-fileserver surface (list_master*, list_states, push/
push_dir/recv) reports the master-minion exclusion explicitly. temp.dir/
file keep scratch space inside the project workspace (.statekit/tmp,
lazy-created) instead of the OS temp directory. xml ports get/set_value
and get/set_attribute over encoding/xml with an ElementTree-subset
finder (bare tag, parent/child, .//descendant, [@attr='value']).
yaml.lint validates structure over gopkg.in/yaml.v3 — upstream's
yamllint style rules stay out of scope; salt:// sources hit the cp
boundary. jinja lands as the minimal data-import surface allowed by the
templating ADR: import_yaml/import_json/load_map parse data files
directly; template logic surfaces honest errors. The data datastore
persists JSON at .statekit/minion/datastore.json with cas/pop/get-list
semantics (upstream serializes msgpack via salt.payload — wire format
divergence documented); defaults ports deepcopy plus dictupdate merge/
update recursion (overlap-triggered recursion, deduplicated list merge)
while defaults.get reports the master boundary. Exec 478→517.

Workspace hygiene: all new write paths stay inside the project tree
(.statekit/, t.TempDir() in suites); system directories are read-only
probe targets at most.

R4.4 landed four families (17 exec functions + the logrotate state).
ret reports its returner-dispatch exclusion per function (the returner
loader is part of the master-minion job architecture). out renders
through json/yaml via internal/output plus a minimal nested renderer;
unknown outputters surface UnsupportedError; string_format strips ANSI
(no-op for these renderers) and html_format wraps escaped text in a
pre block. incron ports list_tab/raw_incron/raw_system_incron/set_job/
rm_job/write_incron_file(+verbose) with the mask-type validation table,
present/new/updated/removed/absent replies, direct system-tab writes
(/etc/incron.d/salt, dir lazy-created) and `incrontab <file>` dispatch
through the Runner for user tabs. logrotate ports the conf parser
(single/multi modes, include recursion with provenance tracking,
script-directive opaque bodies, int coercion), show_conf/get/set_ with
dict guards and prepend-if-not-found line replacement, plus the
logrotate.set_ state (idempotence comment, test mode, old/new changes).
Terminology hygiene: StateKit's own paths and tokens avoid SaltStack
vocabulary — the datastore lives at .statekit/data (was .statekit/
minion); upstream-architecture comments keep Salt terms where they
describe the ported contract. Exec 517→533.

R4.5 landed the status long tail (12 functions via status.RegisterTail):
cpuinfo/cpustats/diskstats/vmstats/netstats/netdev port the Linux
/proc parsers verbatim (field-index mappings preserved, including the
netdev rx-bytes splice at index 1 and the header/row pairing in
/proc/net/netstat); nproc, procs (ps grain command through the Runner
with USER/UID + PID + COMMAND/CMD header-index parsing), w (`w -fh`
row records), time_ (strftime subset converted to Go layouts), the
all_status composite degrading per-probe errors to empty maps, and

probe results (empty without a config delegate). Non-Linux platforms
return empty maps like upstream's platform dispatch. master/
ping_master/proxy_reconnect stay excluded (master-minion). Exec
533→544.

R4.6 landed restartcheck plus the sed/patch file wrappers (4 functions).
restartcheck ports the full pipeline: os_family dispatch (Debian/
RedHat/NILRT with the verbatim unsupported-families dict), kernel
version detection (dpkg --get-selections second-to-last entry rstripped
of the install suffix, then apt-cache policy Installed extraction;
rpm -q kernel for RedHat), running-service correlation via
service.get_running/show delegates, the /proc/PID/maps deleted-file
scanner with LIST_DIRS exclusions and (deleted)/(path inode=N) markers,
package ownership via the pkg.owner delegate with process-name fallback
and owners_cache, init.d/systemd classification through dpkg-query/
repoquery including Type=oneshot filtering and service.available
fallback, check_timeout guards, and both formatter shapes. The /proc
scanner reads the real filesystem (deleted-library detection is a
live-kernel view — documented). file.sed/sed_contains/patch port the
binary-wrapper contracts: _sed_esc quoting rules, shlex-split options,
-i{backup} argv, negate_match, contains' appended p-flag with g default;
patch's which-guard, --forward/--reject-file=- defaults, BSD -C dry-run,
and -d/--strip=0 directory handling. Exec 544→548.

Next in order: E6 is blocked before R8; provide a QEMU/VM runner and populated
`tests/images/vm/` fixtures. R4's renderer boundary remains explicit: Jinja2
uses the bounded Python CLI bridge; gotemplate is opt-in native
`text/template`; file templating and full Salt renderer semantics remain

R9 awaits E5,
R10 cloud, R11 netdev behind ADR gate; pkg provider long tail queued as
its own round; remaining R4 file long-tail slices tracked in the R4
report's pending lists. Master-minion families stay excluded. Docker
sandbox flagged: the daemon's runc cannot spawn containers in this
environment (proc-mount EPERM inside rootless dind); gates ran on the
host toolchain — live openssl interop for tls stayed skipped like the
R5.5 PyNaCl check.

R6.9 ported the Darwin `mac_service` launchd variant (16 public catalog
functions) under the existing `service.*` virtual family. Darwin registration
selects plist discovery over `/Library` and `/System/Library` LaunchAgents/
LaunchDaemons (plus user agents), parses Label/KeepAlive/ProgramArguments
with the standard XML decoder, resolves Salt aliases and basename/full-path
service names, computes system/gui domain targets, and preserves the
launchctl list/enable/disable/bootstrap/bootout/status/print-disabled result
and error shapes. The generic service provider now includes launchd with
kickstart/kill/print/enable/disable operations and Facts selects it from the

`runas` is an explicit boundary because Runtime has no target-user field.
Darwin fixture tests cover plist discovery, service aliases, lifecycle,
KeepAlive/PID status, disabled parsing, missing services and command errors;
the full repository and `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` pass.
Catalog coverage is exec 743→752 (the seven names overlap the generic
service surface), with no host package install and no live macOS runtime in
the current environment.

R7.1 ported the ten public `reg` functions behind a Windows-only build-tag
surface and bootstrap registration: key/value existence and enumeration,
read/set/delete, recursive key deletion, environment broadcast and `.reg`
file import. The Go implementation uses native `reg.exe`/`rundll32` argv
through the central Runner, parses `REG_SZ`/`REG_EXPAND_SZ`/`REG_DWORD`/
`REG_QWORD`/`REG_BINARY`/`REG_MULTI_SZ` output into the Salt result shapes,
preserves default-value handling, 32/64-bit view switches, hive validation,
delete safety checks and `Cannot find` comments, and accepts structured
union-valued registry data through the decoder's `any` support. Volatile
key creation and remote `cp.cache_file` URL resolution remain explicit
boundaries because `reg.exe` cannot express the Win32 API option and the
local-only runtime has no remote fileserver delegate. Windows-only parser
tests and `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c` pass; the full repository
also cross-builds for Windows, while no Windows runtime is attached and no
host package was installed. Catalog coverage is exec 752→762 and `reg`
moves to implemented.

R7.2 ported the Windows `win_useradd` and `win_groupadd` virtual providers
under the existing `user.*`/`group.*` names. Build-time routing selects the
Windows implementation while preserving the Linux and Darwin provider
branches; encoded UTF-16LE/base64 PowerShell scripts reach the central Runner
without shell interpolation of account names/passwords. User operations
cover add/update/delete, SID aliases, password/group membership, home/profile/
full-name changes, info/getent/list/rename/current; group operations cover
add/delete/info/getent/adduser/deluser/members/list_groups. JSON projections
keep Salt's info/getent field shapes and local account/group semantics,
including password/disabled/locked/expiration fields where LocalAccounts
exposes them. Missing accounts map through exit-code 3, sensitive mutation
commands carry redaction values, and the Windows-only fixture tests validate
the encoded command payload, SID/current formatting, JSON fields and not-found
mapping. `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` and user/group test
cross-builds pass; the catalog scanner now accepts mixed-case aliases (so
`user.getUserSid` is measurable); no Windows runtime or host package
installation is available. Catalog coverage is exec 762→770; the virtual
user/group families were already classified implemented.

R7.3 ported the 21 public `win_service` functions behind Windows-only

Windows runtime ceilings; no Windows runtime or host package installation is
available. Catalog coverage is exec 770→779; the service family was already
classified implemented.

R7.4 ported the 20 public `win_pkg` functions behind the Windows `pkg.*`

R5.8 ported the tls family (18 registered exec functions) onto the Go
standard library after the contract read showed pyOpenSSL is a libssl
BINDING, not a CLI wrapper — the substrate mapping is library-to-library
(crypto/x509, encoding/asn1), like R5.4/R5.5, not openssl orchestration.
create_ca generates the RSA key (reuse + `.unloadable.<ts>` rename of
unloadable material), serials ride the `_new_serial` hexlify(microtime +
"_" + urandom) algorithm appended decimal to `<cachedir>/<ca>.serial`
(cachedir via config.option, workspace-local default), certs carry
basicConstraints/pathlen:0 + keyCertSign,cRLSign (critical) plus SKI and
keyid-AKI, key 0600 / cert 0644, index.txt rows keep the exact
"V\t<YYMMDDHHMMSSZ>\t\t<HEX>\tunknown\t/<subject>\n" tab layout with the
subject in upstream wire order (Go typed-field order matches
pyOpenSSL's set order; emailAddress rides ExtraNames). create_csr
reproduces get_extensions' merge (defaults + pillar.get override,
KeyError for unknown profiles), non-critical basicConstraints/keyUsage/
extendedKeyUsage plus text-form subjectAltName parsing (DNS/IP/email/
URI — GeneralNames DER hand-built; double-separator csr_path lives in
paths while messages use single-separator join like upstream
os.path.join). create_ca_signed_cert copies CSR extensions verbatim and
keeps the type_ext-without-cert_type empty-dict guard and the
'There is no CSR that matches the CN "<cert_filename>"' quirk (upstream
replies with cert_filename, not csr_filename). maybe_fix_ssl_version
needed a raw-ASN.1 TBS probe: Go rejects version fields >2 on parse, so
the illegal old-salt literal 3 is detected via tbsPeek (SPKI as one
wrapped field, matching crypto/x509's own parser layout) and subject/
validity extract from the raw DER. cert_info pins the upstream fixture's
OpenSSL goldens (fingerprint colon-hex, "sha256WithRSAEncryption", epoch
dates, huge serial) and renders the family's own extension profile back
into OpenSSL text (keyUsage bit names, EKU long names, SAN with "IP
Address:" forms, SKI/AKI colon-hex). CRL flows (create_empty_crl,
revoke_cert, validate) use x509.CreateRevocationList (CRLNumber=1
documented: Go requires it, cryptography omits it), rebuild from
index.txt R rows with the 159-bit serial truncation on both builders and
validate's lookup key, and revoke_cert reproduces the V→R file.replace
inline (regex-escape replace, backup=False) with Python line iteration
keeping "\n" inside the substring match. validate ports the
X509StoreContext checks reachable in single-CA hierarchies with OpenSSL
reason strings (expired/not-yet-valid/issuer-mismatch/signature) and
error_cert as PEM text instead of an object handle. Documented
boundaries: create_pkcs12 surfaces an explicit unsupported-serialization
error because golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0 ships pkcs12 decode only (the
encoder subpackage is unreleased — hand-rolling a PKCS#12 envelope
without interop verification was rejected); CA certs carry keyid-only
AKI (Go's flat field), leafs gain a Go-added AKI upstream omitted; the
None-base quirk stays (unconfigured base path renders literal
"None/..."); onlyif/unless run through the central Runner's shell like
cmd.retcode; serials >int64 render as exact JSON numbers but quoted YAML
scalars. Two parser-bug classes were caught by tests: PEM must be
decoded before the DER probes, and composite literals in if-init
positions (fixed by caExistsImpl/maybeFixImpl extraction). Exec
618→636.

R5.10 classified the two source implementations hidden behind the public
`x509` family label (ADR 0003). The legacy `salt/modules/x509.py` surface
(40 catalog functions) is an explicit terminal exclusion: it is deprecated
since Salt 3006, announced for removal in 3009, and its contract is bound to
M2Crypto's ctypes ABI plus an openssl CLI parser workaround. The modern
`salt/modules/x509_v2.py` replacement (37 catalog functions, default in Salt
3008) remains planned rather than excluded: local key/PEM/certificate/CSR/CRL
operations are viable on the existing Go crypto substrate, while PKCS#12
(cryptography 36/37 compatibility variants), PKCS#7 (cryptography 37), broad
OpenSSL extension syntax, policy merging and peer signing need a dedicated
round and explicit interop gates. x509 and x509_v2 both serialize as
`module: x509` in the current catalog, so `docs/catalog/compatibility.yaml`
intentionally keeps the collapsed family in `planned` instead of falsely
marking the modern replacement excluded. No dependency or environment
package change was made; x/crypto v0.55.0 has no PKCS#12 encoder or PKCS#7
serializer, and the docker sandbox remains unavailable because rootless dind
cannot mount `/proc` for child containers. The legacy exclusion and modern
upgrade path are recorded in `docs/adr/0003-x509-boundary.md`.

R6.1 ported the four public `macdefaults` functions (`write`, `read`,
`delete`, `cast_value_to_vtype`) behind Darwin-only platform declarations.
The defaults export/import flow uses the central Runner's explicit shell
model; an encoding/xml plist reader/writer preserves strings, bools,

date/data/dict/array validation and exact error wording; XML output is
deterministically key-sorted for fixture stability. The decoder gained the

plist values), with its own regression test. `user`/runas remains an

field; binary plist export is rejected rather than silently misparsed.

cross-builds the package successfully. Catalog coverage is exec 647→651
and macdefaults moves to implemented; the R6 track remains open. The
container sandbox still cannot spawn child containers due rootless-dind

R6.2 ported the Darwin `mac_user` and `mac_group` virtual-provider surfaces

home/full-name/group changes, rename and auto-login enable/disable; the

uses `.` without the node prefix. Runtime filesystem writes preserve the

remain green and `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=amd64 go test -c` builds both packages.
The catalog scanner now deduplicates platform-overlapping virtual names
(`user.*`/`group.*`) so coverage lists remain auditable; exec coverage is
651→664. R6 remains open and no host packages were installed; the configured
rootless dind sandbox still fails before process start on `/proc` mount EPERM.

R6.3 ported the eight public `mac_pkgutil`/`macpackage` functions behind
Darwin-only registrations: pkgutil list/is_installed/install/forget and
macpackage installer/app/mount/unmount/package-list/package-ID helpers.
Native `pkgutil`, `installer`, `hdiutil`, `rsync`, `xar`, `find` and
PlistBuddy invocations are routed through the central Runner, using argv

maps, mount returns the output/mountpoint pair, package identifiers support

The `list_` Salt alias registers as `pkgutil.list`; all functions declare
Darwin platform scope. Linux fake-runner tests cover command shapes,
scheme/file guards, wildcard handling, package-ID fallback and cleanup;
Darwin cross-builds pass. Catalog coverage is exec 664→676 and the
`pkgutil`/`macpackage` families move to implemented; Homebrew/Ports remain
the next R6.4 slice. No host packages were installed; the configured
rootless dind sandbox still fails before process start on `/proc` mount EPERM.

R6.5 ported the five public `mac_desktop` and fifteen public
`mac_softwareupdate` functions behind Darwin-only registrations. Desktop
volume/screen/session/say operations use shell-free `osascript`, `open`,
CGSession and `say` argv with Salt's combined stderr/stdout command-error
text. Software Update supports modern (Label/Title/Version/Action) and
legacy parenthesized output parsers, recommended/restart/shut-down filters,
ignore/reset, schedule status and enable/disable (including the documented
empty-enable readback), update/download single and all flows, downloaded
`.dist` discovery through Runtime.FS, and catalog get/set/reset. Native
commands remain behind the central Runner; fake-runner fixtures cover both
macOS output generations, filters, scheduling, catalog lookup and guards;
`GOOS=darwin GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` passes. Catalog classification
moves desktop and softwareupdate to implemented and exec coverage is
687→707. No host packages were installed; rootless dind still cannot start
child containers because runc hits `/proc` mount EPERM.

R6.6 ported the five public `mac_xattr` functions (`list`, `read`, `write`,
`delete`, `clear`) behind a Darwin-only registration, with the upstream
`list_` alias exposed as `xattr.list`. Native xattr list/read/write/delete/
clear calls use shell-free argv through the central Runner; list composes
per-attribute reads, `-x` stays an explicit flag, write verifies the
post-write value, and error text maps missing files/attributes to Salt's
`File not found`/`Attribute not found`/`Unknown Error` contracts. Invalid
UTF-8 output is replaced like the Python decode path. Fake-runner tests cover
stateful lifecycle, hex flags, errors and platform declarations; coverage is
exec 707→712 and xattr moves to implemented. No host packages were installed;
rootless dind still fails before process start on `/proc` mount EPERM.

R6.7 ported the eight public `mac_keychain` functions behind a Darwin-only
registration: certificate install/uninstall, certificate listing, PKCS#12
friendly-name/hash extraction, default-keychain get/set, and keychain unlock.
`security` and the OpenSSL/grep inspection pipelines run through the central
Runner; password-bearing commands carry Runner redaction entries, improving
on Salt's plaintext-job warning without changing returned values. Default
keychain/user switching is an explicit boundary because the current Runner
has no target-user field; no silent privilege escalation is attempted. Tests
cover argv/shell command shapes, redaction, list/friendly/hash parsing,
unlock/default operations and the boundary. The classifier's former broad
`HasPrefix("key")` rule was corrected to an exact master-minion `key` rule so
local `keychain` is not falsely excluded; the regression is covered by the
catalog tool tests. Keychain moves to implemented and exec coverage is
712→720. No host packages were installed; rootless dind still fails before
process start on `/proc` mount EPERM.

R6.8 ported the eighteen public `mac_power` functions and five public
`mac_assistive` functions behind Darwin-only registrations. `power` mirrors
Salt's `systemsetup` sleep/volume-independent settings, colon-output parser,
minute validation (1–180 or Never/Off), enabled normalization, five-attempt
confirmation polling and exact invalid-value messages; all get/set sleep,
wake, restart and power-button operations use the central Runner. `assistive`
uses the native sqlite3 Runner rather than adding a Go SQLite driver: it
hashes the TCC access schema, handles Mojave/Catalina allowed, Big Sur auth,
and Sonoma branches, issues parameter-escaped installed/enabled queries and
schema-specific insert/update/delete statements, and retries readonly
database writes with the upstream tries/wait semantics. Error wrappers keep
the app-id-specific Salt messages; the `enable_` alias is exposed as
`assistive.enable`. Stateful fake-sqlite/power tests cover all schema columns,
retry, lifecycle, parser, validation and platform declarations; full Linux
gates and `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` pass. Catalog coverage is
exec 720→743 and assistive/power move to implemented. TCC/systemsetup access
was not run on a host, and no packages were installed; rootless dind still
cannot start child containers because runc hits `/proc` mount EPERM.

R6.4 ported the Homebrew/Ports package-provider surface behind Darwin-only
`pkg.*` registration and fact-driven dispatch: the existing `pkg.Register`
selects the mac implementation on Darwin while Linux keeps its provider
functions, and `providers/pkg` now resolves `brew` and `port` managers from
Facts. The common lifecycle covers homebrew_prefix, list_pkgs, version,
latest_version, remove, refresh_db, install, list_upgrades,
upgrade_available and upgrade for both managers; Homebrew's additional
info_installed, hold/unhold (pin/unpin aliases), and list_trusted/trust/
untrust/is_trusted surfaces include JSON v2/v1 parsing, cask/formula aliases,
tap handling, pinned state result maps, and trust-type validation. Ports
parsing keeps active-only `port installed` rows, `@version` normalization,
selfupdate and outdated/upgrade command shapes. Version pins use the native
`@` form for both managers. Runner calls remain argv-based and no package
was installed in the host environment; Darwin cross-build fixtures cover
brew/port selection and JSON/list parsing, while Linux provider tests cover
the new selectors. Catalog coverage is exec 664→687; `pkg` was already an
implemented virtual family, so compatibility classification remains stable.
R6 remains open and the rootless dind sandbox still fails before process
start on `/proc` mount EPERM.
R6 partial addendum (timezone.zone_compare Linux-generic sub-slice,
PTD-EXEC-1638/PTD-TEST-1673; both rows stay open): the Linux-only
filesystem contract of zone_compare landed in `modules/exec/timezone`
behind a PlatformConstrained [linux] registration. Validation runs
before any filesystem access: nonempty relative ASCII names of
`[A-Za-z0-9_+-]` components, <=1024 total bytes, <=255-byte segments,
<=64 components; absolute names, backslash, controls/NUL, empty, `.`,
`..`, repeated/trailing slash are rejected and the input is never
trimmed or normalized, so UTC, Etc/GMT+5, Etc/GMT-14, US/Eastern,
America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires and EST5EDT survive. Fast detection
uses /etc/timezone only as a regular file through the bounded
no-follow `runtime.ReadFileBounded` (symlink/special/oversize skipped
in favor of /etc/localtime) and a contained /etc/localtime symlink
yielding the exact name from the initial target — alias preserved —
with an exact case-sensitive compare where unequal answers false with
no byte fallback. Only on detection error does a bounded byte fallback
run, reading /etc/localtime first (its execution-category error wins)
and then /usr/share/zoneinfo/<zone> (invocation-category error when
unusable). Symlink chains resolve component-wise (Lstat/Readlink only)
inside the fixed /usr/share/zoneinfo root with max 8 hops / 64
cumulative components (prefix included), rejecting escape, loop,
dangling, special-file, and directory finals; content reads are
bounded at 1 MiB and fail closed when the filesystem lacks the bounded
capability (never raw FS.ReadFile for timezone files). Errors are
fixed and value-free only — `unknown/unsafe zone` (invocation
category, SaltInvocationError analog) and `cannot determine current
zone` (execution category, CommandExecutionError analog) with
errors.Is sentinels; no commands, Runner calls, writes, or
dependencies. Documented divergences/ceilings: no timedatectl fast
detection (Runner-free slice), a dangling /etc/localtime target fails
closed instead of yielding Salt's readlink-only name, /etc/localtime
symlinks must resolve under /usr/share/zoneinfo (hosts pointing
elsewhere fail closed with the execution error), the 64-component
budget counts the zoneinfo prefix so deeper-but-valid names fail
resolution, no atomic snapshot across the walk, and /etc plus
/usr/share/zoneinfo parents/mounts are assumed admin-controlled.
Explicitly out of scope: the `_get_localtime_path` NILinuxRT special
case (unsupported ceiling), mac_timezone.py, win_timezone.py, and the
Solaris/AIX string-only variants — the aggregate PTD-EXEC-1638 row,
PTD-TEST-1673, and the R6 native/Darwin report remain open/partial.

R6 Windows partial plan addendum (timezone.zone_compare Windows
variant, PTD-EXEC-1638/PTD-TEST-1673; both rows REMAIN open/partial —
HISTORICAL PRE-IMPLEMENTATION DESIGN SNAPSHOT: this was the plan-only
record written for QA-gate re-review before implementation, when
nothing of the Windows variant was implemented, registered, or
claimed; it is superseded by the later committed Windows
implementation record below (commit `331790b` "feat(timezone): add
Windows zone comparison"), which implements and registers the design
recorded here; the snapshot is retained for its decision/acceptance
history and claims no full aggregate-row completion): the Linux TZC
and Mac MZC phases above were already committed when this snapshot
was written; this subsection records the detailed Windows-only design
the QA gate re-reviewed before the implementation phase opened. This
revision resolved the four blocking QA re-gate gaps: pinned sentinel
categories with the errors.Is contract, explicit zero-exit truncation
and exact-cap cases, the WZC-GAP-01..09 source-gap crosswalk, and the
named mandatory implementation/commit gates. No code, tests, catalog
regeneration, or workflow change accompanied the plan phase this
snapshot records; `.github`, go.mod/go.sum, LICENSE/NOTICE, ADR 0004,
and the MySQL Containerfile were explicitly out of scope for that
plan phase.

Plan of record (Windows-only; executor per item):

1. Source contract (backend-engineer-senior): the full static
   timezone-name map of exactly 134 Windows/IANA pairs is ported
   verbatim from pinned `saltstack/salt/modules/win_timezone.py`
   lines 46–183 (pinned revision per `references/salt.lock`); no
   CLDR data, no new Go module dependency, no generated catalog.
   Do-not-trim is normative: user input is never trimmed or
   normalized; the source invalid-timezone error is execution-
   category but the StateKit message stays value-free; an unknown
   nonempty current tzutil answer yields false, not an error.
2. Windows resolution path (backend-engineer-senior; plan/security
   review by solution-architect-lead and security-architect-lead):
   the existing golang.org/x/sys v0.47.0 (`x/sys/windows`)
    `GetSystemDirectory` plus machine-wide `GetSystemWindowsDirectory`
    supply the system tree — per-user `GetWindowsDirectory` is never
    used — and any API error or malformed result fails closed with
    `ErrCannotDetermineZone`; the returned systemdir must be an
    absolute, lexically clean local
   drive path whose immediate child is exactly System32 or SysWOW64
   (case-insensitive); UNC, device, extended-length, drive-relative,
   root-relative, traversal, sibling, and deeper paths are rejected.
   Dispatch reuses the existing central Runner unchanged.
3. Exact-exec boundary (security-architect-lead, concurred by
   solution-architect-lead): Go 1.26.6 still consults the parent
    PATHEXT even for an absolute executable path, so an exact `Lstat`
    of `tzutil.exe` runs immediately before Runner dispatch and
    requires a regular, non-reparse file; absent, inaccessible,
    reparse, or non-regular answers `ErrCannotDetermineZone` with
    zero dispatch. This defeats PATHEXT suffix fallback ONLY under the
   explicit assumption of an admin-controlled system tree with no
   unprivileged replacement; the plan must NOT claim unconditional
   exact exec, and the admin-controlled-tree/TOCTOU residual is
   documented as accepted.
4. Dispatch shape (backend-engineer-senior): exactly one shell-free
   `tzutil.exe /g` per invocation — absolute executable name, argv
   exactly [/g], Dir=systemdir, Env only API-derived SYSTEMROOT/
   WINDIR, Shell=false, empty WindowsCmdLine, no user input in argv
   or env; stdout/stderr capped at 64 KiB each; the 30s timeout is
    the cancellation deadline, not a strict end-to-end cap (Runner
    WaitDelay); nonzero exit, Runner error, cancellation, deadline,
    truncation, or over-cap each fail closed with
    `ErrCannotDetermineZone`. State output never
    mutates the filesystem or registry.
5. Sentinel contract (backend-engineer-senior): the Windows variant
   exposes exactly two distinct fixed execution-category sentinels
   with exact value-free messages, and the required gate is
   three-way. First the required-argument gate: an omitted `timezone`
   key or a nil `winZoneCompareArgs.TimeZone` pointer fails args
   decoding with `config.MissingRequiredError` before any resolver/
   Lstat/Runner work — never `ErrInvalidWindowsZone`.
   `ErrInvalidWindowsZone` (exact message "invalid Windows timezone")
   is returned only for: a wrong dynamic argument type or a typed-nil
   args value reaching direct `Execute` (safety guards), an explicit
   nonnil empty string, or any nonempty name with no case-insensitive
   match in the 134-pair table in the requested-name gate (input is
   never trimmed or normalized before the match).
   `ErrCannotDetermineZone` (the existing package
   sentinel, exact message "cannot determine current zone") covers
   every query/execution failure: resolver API error or malformed
   systemdir, precheck failure (tzutil.exe absent/inaccessible/
   reparse/non-regular), Runner error, nonzero retcode,
   cancellation/deadline, truncation or over-cap, and an
   empty-after-rstrip current-query stdout. `errors.Is` contract:
   each returned error matches exactly its intended sentinel and
   never the other — every invalid-input error (wrong/typed-nil
   direct-call args, explicit empty string, unlisted requested name)
   satisfies errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidWindowsZone) and NOT
   errors.Is(err, ErrCannotDetermineZone), and query/execution
   failures satisfy errors.Is(err, ErrCannotDetermineZone) and NOT
   errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidWindowsZone); neither sentinel ever
   wraps a raw cause, and no returned error text includes the
   timezone name, systemdir path, command output, stderr, underlying
   error text, or exit code. Ordering: the required-argument gate
   runs before any resolver/Lstat/Runner work, and the requested-name
   gate runs strictly before the resolver API calls and before the
   Lstat precheck, so invalid input never dispatches and never
   touches the resolver; query failures issue at most the single
   `/g` dispatch and are never retried.
6. Output processing (backend-engineer-senior): Python `str.rstrip()`
   whitespace semantics (CRLF, tab, U+00A0, U+0085, U+2028, U+3000,
   U+001C..U+001F), leading whitespace preserved; the empty-after-
   rstrip check is defined as: after stripping every trailing
   character in the rstrip whitespace set, the captured stdout is
   zero-length (an empty or whitespace-only answer) and returns
   `ErrCannotDetermineZone`. The value is lowercased then exactly one
   terminal `_dstoff` suffix is removed (repeated-suffix input pinned
   by test). Zero-exit truncation fails closed even when the capture
   is otherwise valid: with exit code 0 and a valid zone name in
   stdout, `StdoutTruncated=true` must return only
   `ErrCannotDetermineZone`, and `StderrTruncated=true` with an
   otherwise valid stdout must also return only
   `ErrCannotDetermineZone` — never the parsed value, never
   `ErrInvalidWindowsZone`. The cap boundary is exact: a stdout
   capture of exactly 65536 bytes (64 KiB) is accepted when its
   rstripped content is a valid zone, and 65537 bytes is rejected
   with `ErrCannotDetermineZone`.
7. Notice/licensing item (compliance-officer-senior check;
   release-manager-senior follow-up): the root NOTICE is a required
   deliverable of the implementation phase — retain saltstack/NOTICE
   verbatim, separately retain `Copyright (c) 2011-2022 VMware, Inc.`
   and `Copyright: 2014 SaltStack Team` with their origins (date
   ranges are never merged), and add the exact source path/commit/
   adaptation note; the root LICENSE is unchanged; actual binary
   release packages must ship LICENSE/NOTICE before any release.
8. Registration (backend-engineer-senior): Linux and Darwin variant
   arguments/behavior are unchanged; the Windows variant is selected
   exactly once; an unsupported GOOS leaves the name unregistered
   (never registered-but-unsupported); duplicate registration is
   rejected.
9. Verification gates (qa-engineer-senior): the WZC-01..18 acceptance
   matrix and the WZC-GAP crosswalk below pin source/acceptance;
   compile-only `GOOS=windows GOARCH={amd64,386,arm64}` builds plus
   the other existing cross-build variants gate the phase —
   compile-only, never native execution.

WZC acceptance matrix (numbered, concise, testable;
qa-engineer-senior owns the gate):

- WZC-01 Required-gate boundary: an omitted `timezone` key or nil
  required `*string` pointer fails with `config.MissingRequiredError`
  before resolver/Lstat/Runner; explicit nonnil empty and unlisted
  names return only `ErrInvalidWindowsZone` (not
  `ErrCannotDetermineZone`) before resolver/dispatch, zero calls.
- WZC-02 Exact case-insensitive match of valid input in both Windows
  and IANA forms; input is never trimmed.
- WZC-03 All 134 pinned pairs exactly match source with no duplicate
  lowercase keys or values, round-trip in both directions, full sweep
  in both input forms; anchors: India/Calcutta, Mountain/Denver_dstoff,
  FLE/Kiev, and the UTC sign mapping.
- WZC-04 Unknown nonempty current zone output returns false.
- WZC-05 Output matrix: Python str.rstrip whitespace set (CRLF, tab,
  U+00A0, U+0085, U+2028, U+3000, U+001C..U+001F), leading whitespace
  preserved, empty-after-rstrip errors (defined as: after stripping
  all trailing rstrip-whitespace characters the captured stdout is
  zero-length — empty or whitespace-only — and returns
  `ErrCannotDetermineZone`), lowercase-then-strip of
  exactly one terminal `_dstoff` including a repeated suffix.
- WZC-06 Direct wrong dynamic args type or typed-nil args returns
  fixed `ErrInvalidWindowsZone` with no panic/resolver/Lstat/Runner;
  the missing required field is the separate
  `config.MissingRequiredError` from WZC-01; a counting Runner
  verifies zero calls.
- WZC-07 Only GetSystemDirectory + machine-wide
  GetSystemWindowsDirectory are used (never per-user
  GetWindowsDirectory); errors/malformed results fail closed with
  `ErrCannotDetermineZone`.
- WZC-08 Systemdir validation: absolute clean local drive paths with
  the exact case-insensitive System32/SysWOW64 immediate child;
  UNC/device/extended/drive-relative/root-relative/traversal/sibling/
  deeper paths rejected.
- WZC-09 Exact `Lstat` of `tzutil.exe` immediately before Runner
  dispatch, requiring regular/non-reparse; absent/inaccessible/
  reparse/non-regular yield `ErrCannotDetermineZone` with zero
  dispatch.
- WZC-10 Hostile PATHEXT: with the exact executable present the path
  stays exact; with the exact file missing but `tzutil.exe.com`/
  `tzutil.exe.cmd` siblings present the precheck fails with zero
  dispatch; admin-controlled-tree/TOCTOU residual explicitly
  documented (no unconditional exact-exec claim).
- WZC-11 Exact command fields: absolute name, argv [/g],
  Dir=systemdir, Env only API-derived SYSTEMROOT/WINDIR, Shell=false,

Authorization of record (target/scope/approver/source timestamp):
the user's direct 2026-10-05T11:01:35Z statement approves exactly
this target — the StateKit CLI function `timezone.get_zonecode`
resolving the fixed `date` executable via the caller/deployment's

and exactly this scope: one fixed no-argument `date +%Z` dispatch
through the process Runner with `Name="date"`, `Args=["+%Z"]`,
`Shell=false`, `Dir="/"`, child `Env` exactly `LC_ALL=C` plus caller

Compatibility/safety ceilings (accepted divergences from the pinned
Salt behavior): every Runner error, nonzero exit, truncation flag,
over-cap capture, cancellation, and deadline maps to the fixed
value-free `ErrZonecodeQuery` (new sentinel) with nil output — Salt
`cmd.run` normally returns stdout even on nonzero retcode and merges
stderr (`subprocess.STDOUT`), so fail-closed mapping is an
intentional safer divergence; child `Env` replaces inheritance
(`LC_ALL=C` and `TZ` only — `TZDIR`, other loader/locale variables,
and any secrets present in the caller env are omitted), and the fixed
`Dir=/` is an intentional divergence from Salt's cwd default: per
`saltstack/salt/modules/cmdmod.py:367-380`, Salt `cmd.run` defaults
the working directory to the Minion/runas user's home directory
(`os.path.expanduser("~<runas>")`) and falls back to `/` (Windows:
`os.path.abspath(os.sep)`) only when that home is unreadable or not a
directory — it is not a simply inherited cwd; the returned
abbreviation and all error details are never logged.
