serial-number parsing, TTL/not_before/not_after handling, principals,
critical-options/extensions, raw/string/path output and copypath; the
certificate wire bytes are verified against x/crypto's own bytes-for-signing
layout and authorized-key parser. create_private_key covers RSA/EC/
Ed25519 generation, OpenSSH PEM encoding (encrypted and unencrypted),
0600/0644 path writes, public-key sidecar and overwrite guard; the
pubkey_suffix empty string is the local equivalent of upstream's false
skip switch. encode_private_key round-trips encrypted keys and preserves
the upstream missing/wrong/passphrase error messages. expires,
get_private_key_size, get_public_key, verify_private_key and
verify_signature port the introspection/cryptographic checks; read_certificate
returns cert_type/principals/key-id/type/size, colon-hex serial, UTC dates,
key lines, critical options/extensions and SHA-256 plus non-FIPS MD5
fingerprints. get_signing_policy and sign_remote_certificate reproduce
the local pillar-over-config lookup and policy merge: forced/default/
allowed option and extension maps, principal intersection/defaults,
TTL/max-TTL clamping and policy precedence; policy-only responses strip
private key material and expose signing_public_key. `ca_server`,
_query_remote, compound matching and __pub_id are explicit boundaries:
peer publish is master-minion architecture and unavailable in StateKit's
local-only runtime; matcher policies return the upstream
"minion sending this request could not be identified" response. The Go
SSH library supplies bcrypt-backed encrypted-key parsing/encoding, so no
environment package installation or new dependency was needed. Tests
cover RSA/EC/Ed25519 and certificate round-trips, signature tampering,
policy precedence, encrypted-key failures, path modes, expiry and all
remote boundary/error shapes. Exec 636→647.

R5.7 completed the gpg module with its key-management tail (12 registered
exec functions), all through the gpg CLI with --with-colons streams:
list_keys/list_secret_keys filter pub/sec records by mode and render the
python-gnupg key shape (keyid/fingerprint/uids, %Y-%m-%d created/expires
with the expired boolean, keyLength, letter-trust translations);
get_key/get_secret_key keep the short-id slice quirk (long[8:]); read_key
maps to gpg --show-keys with path/text exclusivity guards; search_keys
and receive_keys talk to keys.openpgp.org by default with IMPORT_OK code
messages (added/already-exists/updated-new-signatures/updated-new-subkeys)
and IMPORT_PROBLEM fallbacks; import_key carries both invocation errors,
the fingerprints list plus Successfully-imported/already-exist/unable
message mapping and the 3008 select filter via a temp.file throwaway
keyring roundtrip; export_key reproduces bare/output/comment shapes with
loopback passphrases for secret material; create_key generates the batch
parameter file (Key-Type/Length, names, subkey halves, Expire-Date,
%no-protection or Passphrase) and reads KEY_CREATED for the fingerprint;
delete_key keeps the argument guards, secret-first ordering with
"Secret key exists..." refusal and the deleted/failed message pairs;
trust_key validates exactly-one-of and the six trust levels, then drives
--import-ownertrust through a stdin-substitute file parsing the from/to
digits into "Changing ownership trust"/"Setting ownership trust" replies.
A prefix-handling bug class was caught by tests across all status parsers:
field indices must be taken after stripping "[GNUPG:] ". The gpg family is
now fully registered modulo upstream's own library dependencies (exec
606→618).

R5.6 ported the gpg cryptographic core (4 registered exec functions)
driving the real gpg binary through the central Runner with --status-fd 2
instead of python-gnupg: encrypt/decrypt keep upstream's {"res","comment"}
dicts (bare mode returns raw strings; output targets flip the comment to
"Encrypted/Decrypted data has been written to ..."), sign returns the
armored block with --local-user keyid support and loopback passphrases;
verify parses GOODSIG/EXPKEYSIG/VALIDSIG/TRUST_*/ERRSIG status lines into
the sig_info shape and implements both return contracts — the single-key
trust dict ("The signature is verified." with username/key_id/trust_level
mapped through the gnupg>=0.5.1 table) and the 3007 multi-key matrix
(signed_by_any short-circuit message, signed_by_all per-key failure text,
"All required keys have provided a signature") plus the trustmodel
validation list. Homedir machinery ports _get_user_info (config-user
fallback), _get_user_gnupghome ("salt" user -> config_dir/gpgkeys,
GNUPGHOME via environ.get, ~/.gnupg fallback) and the 0700 creation
recovery of _create_gpg; ownership fix-ups degrade to root-only chown
under the StateKit single-user model. Passphrases resolve from
config.get("gpg_passphrase") with the verbatim pillar error. Key
management remains pending for R5.7 (exec 602→606).

R5.5 unblocked nacl via ADR 0002 (owner-approved use of the standard Go
crypto extension library) and ported the family on golang.org/x/crypto
v0.55.0 (9 registered exec functions): keygen reproduces the branch
matrix verbatim — keypair dict when file-less, "saved sk_file:"/"saved
pk_file:"/the double-space pair message, both-exist and pk-without-sk
errors — deriving public keys through X25519(sk, basepoint); sealedbox_
encrypt/decrypt ride box.SealAnonymous/OpenAnonymous for crypto_box_seal
wire compatibility; secretbox_encrypt/decrypt reproduce libnacl's layout
(24-byte nonce prepended to crypto_secretbox_easy output, injectable
nonce source for hermetic wire assertions); enc/dec route by box_type
(default sealedbox) over the config.get("nacl.config") merge with a
workspace-local pki_dir fallback; enc_file/dec_file resolve inputs via
cp.get_file_str first with local-FS fallback and keep the out-exists
guard; dec returns None for None input; FIPS-mode refusal ports the
__virtual__ gate. Key material length checks reject short keys where
PyNaCl would raise. go.mod expands for the first time since R1: x/crypto
plus indirect x/sys v0.47.0; the audit procedure re-ran per ADR 0002 —
version-pinned OSV shows only GO-2026-5932 against the unmaintained
x/crypto/openpgp subpackage, proven absent from the build graph via
go list -deps/go mod why; go mod verify clean; live PyNaCl interop was
intentionally not executed (no packages installed into the environment
without approval) — wire compatibility rests on the shared primitives
and is structurally pinned by tests. Exec 593→602.

R5.4 ported the asymmetric family onto the Go standard library (2
registered exec functions, zero new dependencies): asymmetric.sign loads
PKCS#8/PKCS#1/SEC1 private keys (legacy DEK-Info encryption honored with
a passphrase; OpenSSH containers and Ed448 surface explicit unsupported-
algorithm errors) and signs text or file inputs — RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 and
ECDSA ASN.1 consume the single file digest (prehashed), Ed25519 signs raw
bytes; output is base64 by default with raw=true defaulting to bool(path)
and the "Signature written to '...'" path reply. asymmetric.verify keeps
the gpg.verify-compatible {"res","message"} contract: mutual-exclusion and
missing-parameter invocation errors verbatim, signature references via
inline base64/local paths/file:// plus cp.cache_file for remote schemes,
plain pubkey+signature degrading into signed_by_all=[pubkey] exactly like
upstream, signed_by_any short-circuit with its none-matched message,
signed_by_all consuming one signature per key, and cached file digests so
multi-key checks hash the input once. Tests generate RSA-2048/P-256/
Ed25519 keys at runtime with stdlib crypto and pin roundtrips, tamper
rejection, multi-check matrices and every guard text (exec 591→593).

R5.3 shipped the small CLI/FS batch of the security round (9 registered
exec functions across three new packages): the acl package registers
under Salt's virtual name with version/getfacl/wipefacls/modfacl/delfacl —
getfacl ports the comment-header grammar (# file:/owner:/group:/flags:)
into upstream's nested entry shape including suid/sgid/sticky flag
decoding and default: rule separation, _parse_acl derives octal from
rwx strings with owner/group fallbacks, mod/del/wipe build setfacl argv
with -R-before--m ordering, d:g prefix normalization and the verbatim
no-files guard; missing binaries surface the __virtual__ message. The
pam package reads /etc/pam.d-style files through the FS abstraction,
porting the bracketed control-flag continuation ("[success=1
default=ignore]") into interface/control_flag/module/arguments rules
with the literal False missing-file reply. The webutil package wraps
htpasswd useradd/userdel/verify through the central Runner: create-flag
appending for absent files, run_all dict vs stdout-lines shapes, the
retcode==0 verify contract and the verbatim which-guard message.
Upstream has no unit tests for these three surfaces; hermetic fake-Runner
fixtures pin every flow (exec 582→591).

R5.2 completed the ssh module's authorized-keys surface (10 registered
exec functions): _validate_keys ports the options/enc/key/comment line
grammar over an RE2 translation of upstream's patterns; auth_keys keeps
the single-user old shape and silently skips unresolvable users;
check_key runs the refine_enc normalization (rsa/dss/ecdsa/ed25519 plus
the cert-v01 and sk- allowlist) against the formatted-line comparison;
set_auth_key carries the full guard chain — multiword "invalid", unknown
user "fail", base64-validity "Invalid public key", homedir-must-exist
"fail" — then dir creation 0700/new-file 0600 with root-only chown and
best-effort restorecon through the Runner; _replace_auth_key rewrites
matching key lines preserving comments; rm_auth_key reproduces the
documented quirk that unparseable non-key lines are dropped during the
rewrite ("Key removed"/"Key not present"/"Key not removed" verdicts);
*_from_file variants layer cp.cache_file resolution and the fail >
replace > new > no-change aggregation order; check_key_file maps keys to
add/update/exists; host_keys scans ssh_host_*_key files with private/
certs filters and the FORMAT 1.1 binary guard; user_keys walks the
id_{rsa,dsa,ecdsa,ed25519} defaults under ~/.ssh with tri-state
pubfile/prvfile overrides and empty-user pruning; key_is_encrypted pins
the Proc-Type ENCRYPTED probe with the not-a-private-key error. A
Python-vs-RE2 anchoring divergence was caught by tests and fixed: lines
are matched stripped because RE2 `$` does not tolerate a trailing newline
like Python's. The ssh family is now fully registered modulo its
excluded/pending tails (exec 572→582).

R5.1 opened the security round with the ssh known-hosts surface (6
registered exec functions): get_known_host_entries runs ssh-keygen -F
through the central Runner with the which-guard carrying upstream's
CommandNotFoundError text verbatim and parses via _parse_openssh_output
(three-field lines, comment/whitespace skips, strict-base64 fingerprints
in RFC 4716 colon form over an injectable hash type defaulting sha256);
recv_known_host_entries assembles the ssh-keyscan argv (-p/-t/-H/-T) with
the five-attempt retry loop and the injectable CentOS-5 osfinger probe;
check_known_host returns add/exists/update plus the hostname-argument
error dict; rm_known_host carries the known-file guards, [host]:port
lookup forms and root-only chown through the user.info delegate; 
set_known_host ports the full decision matrix (port/hash conflict,
fingerprint mismatch against keyscan output, check_required set-equality,
matched-enc line removal via the -F line-number pairs with reverse-order
deletes, mode preservation or 0600 on create, config-dir creation, the
key+hash_known_hosts self-call to hash_known_hosts); hash_known_hosts
preserves mode across the -H rewrite. Known-hosts files go through the
FileSystem abstraction so MemoryFS fixtures pin every flow hermetically;
the None reply contract serializes as null. Divergences documented
in-code: empty-enc rendering instead of Python's literal "None" artifact,
and the stateless replacement of __context__ caching. Upstream has no unit
tests for this surface; contracts pin source behavior directly. The ssh
family stays partial pending the auth-keys half (exec 566→572).

R4.7 landed the managed-source meta family behind file.manage_file (15
registered exec functions): check_file_meta ports the full probe — newfile
detection, hsum-vs-lstats sum comparison with the sfn cache fallback,
contents-diff via tempfiles, obfuscate_templates through config.option,

(upstream's _error contract), makedirs dir-mode derivation OR-ing execute

still writes new-file contents (states gate earlier). check_perms ports the

with suid/sgid mode restoration, post-verification failure texts, attrs

crash (init.md section 28). get_diff ships a faithful difflib port
(SequenceMatcher with autojunk, grouped opcodes, unified_diff headers even
when show_filenames=False) mapped onto the exact upstream test vectors incl.
Cyrillic lines and the binary-replace strings, plus get_conditional_diff.
source_list degrades master lists to empty (master-minion excluded) while

with all four verbatim error texts. FileSystem gains Lchown (OS + memory);

fake Runner; difflib outputs are byte-exact against CPython vectors. File
family remains partial — find/grep/line/diskusage/statvfs/open_files/move/

## 7. Porting Debt Register (audit snapshot)

- **Snapshot:** 2026-08-29; pinned input HEAD `c3e7b8f` (before this documentation edit); pinned Salt `8b63e700637e40d76f80a00d95c60471797c73b9` (`references/salt.lock`).
- **Canonical identity/counts:** loader-visible identity is `kind + canonical module.function`; canonical public catalog totals are **2574** exec and **436** state after deduplication. Generated coverage records raw Go `Name()` inventories as **947** exec and **50** state, alongside catalog intersections of **922** exec and **47** state; these are distinct metrics and neither claims full Jinja parity. The four new raw exec names from the gotemplate additions are `gotemplate.render`, `gotemplate.import_yaml`, `gotemplate.import_json`, and `gotemplate.load_map`; a fifth new raw exec name is `file.apply_template_on_contents`.
- **Executor policy:** actionable implementation and tooling rows are assigned to `software-engineer-senior` (senior software engineer, Go porting/tooling); regression/contract rows to `qa-engineer-senior` (senior QA engineer, Go); documentation rows to `technical-writer-lead` (lead technical writer); excluded classifications to `solution-architect-lead` (lead solution architect). Review requires a senior maintainer plus platform owner for R6-R8.
- **Canonical enumeration algorithm (normative for this snapshot):** (1) parse every concrete catalog and pinned Salt source path named by the function rows below, excluding only source function names beginning `_`; resolve each source file's `__virtualname__` and `__func_alias__`; apply the StateKit family aliases exactly as `tools/salt-reference/catalog.go#familyAliases`; deduplicate by `kind + canonical loader-visible module.function` while preserving every concrete catalog/source/test provenance item in semicolon-separated cells. (2) Compare canonical names with actual non-test Go `Name()` literals and `internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go#BuildRuntime`; record wrong aliases as `noncanonical-registered`, Go-but-unwired names as `registered-missing`, and R6/R7 registered names without a native runner as `registered-but-runtime-unproven`; all other absent public functions are `actionable`. (3) Emit every architecture-only function as `excluded` with its exact local-only ADR reason; emit each non-CLI lifecycle hook once as `deferred` pending a lifecycle-engine ADR and explicit round assignment. (4) Treat the concrete differential report paths named by test rows only as scope evidence; R6/R7 remain cross-build-only until their native tests pass, and retain every mapped Salt source/test path.

##### 2026-09-30 current status (R10.4c private syslog config parsing helper; external CI pending)

R10.4c adds the THIRD vsphere-family surface of the pinned
`salt/modules/vsphere.py` to the existing `modules/exec/vsphere`
package: the unexported `formatSyslogConfig(cmdRet map[string]any)
(map[string]any, error)`, a bounded pure port of `_format_syslog_config`
(pinned lines 7704–7723, `def` through `return`, pinned revision
`8b63e700637e40d76f80a00d95c60471797c73b9`). Nothing is registered:
there is no `Name()`, no bootstrap registration, no public catalog
entry, no registry/counter increment, and no catalog/coverage
regeneration — R10 public totals are UNCHANGED (15 canonical public + 7
dig aliases; dnsutil 10/11 public with `serial` pending; generated R10
report still `round: R10.3b` with 25 registered_public / 1
pending_public / 7 aliases). Like the R10.4a/R10.4b helpers, it is an
internal source-compatible parsing primitive, NOT a usable
vSphere/cloud implementation: it holds no credentials, opens no
endpoint, calls no PyVmomi/govc/vendor CLI, and makes no network or
provider call — real provider transport remains ADR/decision-gated per
the R10 policy (§2/R10: vendor CLI wrappers first; provider connections
are a separate gated decision).

The parser mirrors the pinned source exactly, quirk-inclusive, with
every edge vector confirmed by executing the pinned function itself as
a local oracle: success is DERIVED from `cmd_ret["retcode"] == 0`
(unlike the firewall helper's hardcoded True) — a nonzero retcode
stores `ret_dict["message"] = cmd_ret["stdout"]` verbatim and never
parses lines, a zero retcode starts `{"success": True}` and iterates
`cmd_ret["stdout"].splitlines()`; each line is stripped BEFORE the
split, so a whitespace-only line becomes empty and a whitespace-only
tail disappears before the delimiter search ("a: " strips to "a:" and
is then malformed); `line.split(": ")` is the Python split on the exact
two-character literal ": " (colon + ASCII space), all occurrences, so a
colon followed by a tab or without a trailing space never matches while
"a : b" does with only the second `cfgvars[0].strip()` removing the
interior spaces; only cfgvars[0] and cfgvars[1] are consumed with
longer tails discarded; duplicate keys overwrite in encounter order and
a parsed key "success" overwrites the boolean true with a string; an
empty line is MALFORMED (the pinned IndexError — blank lines are never
skipped, unlike the coredump helper) while empty stdout iterates zero
lines and returns only {"success": true}; and a leading-empty first
field is valid data (": x" stores the empty key ""). This helper runs
no lower(): keys and values keep their exact case and Unicode.
StateKit bounds that the pinned source lacks, fail-closed with fixed
value-free sentinel errors and no partial map on any failure: retcode
must be a Go int (checked first, matching the pinned read order at line
7711) and stdout a string (missing key, nil, or any other type answers
a fixed type error — both fields are read on both pinned paths, so both
types are validated unconditionally before the retcode branch); input
bytes ≤ 64 KiB (checked before UTF-8 validation) and valid UTF-8, both
enforced before the branch so the nonzero message copy is as bounded
and JSON-encodable as the parsed result; at most 1024 lines; each
retained key/value ≤ 4096 bytes post-strip; at most 256 retained
ret_dict entries including the initial success entry, enforced before
insertion (duplicates and the parsed "success" entry overwrite in place
and never grow the map). Mechanically the slice adds NO new helper
machinery: it reuses the shared `pythonSplitlinesBounded` bounded
scanner and the shared `pythonStrip`/`pythonWhitespace` semantics (no
lower(), no bare split()), and `strings.Split` is the exact Go
equivalent of the Python `str.split(": ")`. plans/testing.md needed NO
change: the rootless `r10_contract` command already includes
`./modules/exec/vsphere`, the contract file inventory is unchanged, and
no GitHub workflow was touched.

PyVmomi/govc/vendor CLI, and makes no network or provider call — real

The parser mirrors the pinned source exactly, quirk-inclusive: the
"Name"/"---" startswith skips run on the RAW unstripped, un-lowercased
line (unlike the coredump helper, leading whitespace or case never
produces a skip — "  Name: 1" is stored as data under the exact key
"Name:" and "NAME" is data), Python `str.split()` whitespace semantics
(str.isspace(): Go unicode.IsSpace plus U+001C..U+001F, runs collapsed,
no empty tokens) feed the pinned `rulesets[ruleset_status[0]] =
bool(ruleset_status[1])` store where nonempty-string truthiness makes
every stored value true — the token "false" stores true — only tokens
[0] and [1] are consumed with longer tails discarded, unknown
headings/rules are stored as data, and duplicate names overwrite in
encounter order with plain map semantics. The pinned ret_dict shape is
kept: `{"success": true, "rulesets": {...}}` with success the pinned
hardcoded True, never derived from `cmd_ret["retcode"]`. Empty stdout
iterates zero lines and returns the pinned empty dict with an allocated
ruleset map; a whitespace-only or single-token row raises IndexError in
the pinned source and answers the fixed malformed-row sentinel here.
StateKit bounds that the pinned source lacks, fail-closed with fixed
value-free sentinel errors and no partial result on any failure:
stdout must be a string (missing key, nil, or any non-string type
answers a fixed type error), input bytes ≤ 64 KiB (checked before
UTF-8 validation), stdout must be valid UTF-8, at most 1024 lines
(this loop has no pinned early exit, so every line is reached), each
consumed token ≤ 4096 bytes, and at most 256 retained rulesets
enforced before insertion (duplicates never grow the map). Mechanically,
the R10.4a coredump loop's inline splitlines scanner was extracted into
the shared package-private bounded splitter `pythonSplitlinesBounded`
and rewired behavior-identically (the entire R10.4a tagged suite passes
unchanged, including its exact line-limit boundaries and the 5001-line
short-circuit), and the `str.split()` port follows the dig/dnsutil
`pythonFields` convention. plans/testing.md needed NO change: the
rootless `r10_contract` command already includes
`./modules/exec/vsphere`, the contract file inventory is unchanged, and
no GitHub workflow was touched.

The parser mirrors the pinned source exactly, quirk-inclusive: Python
`str.splitlines()` boundaries (\n, \r, \r\n one boundary, \v, \f,

final-sigma rule is the one documented lowercasing divergence), the
four case-insensitive prefixes (`enabled:`, `host vnic:`,
`network server ip:`, `network server port:`), the SUBSTRING truth test
`"true" in parts[1]` on the UNSTRIPPED second field ("trueish"/"nottrue"
both enable), the pinned `break` that stops parsing immediately on a
false store while keeping all previously stored fields, Python
`split(":")[1]` colon-field indexing kept verbatim (IPv6 values
truncate at the first inner colon, adjacent colons store empty values,
everything past the second colon is discarded — never normalized), and
duplicate recognized fields overwriting in encounter order while
unknown labels and blank lines fall through. StateKit bounds the pinned
source lacks, fail-closed with fixed value-free sentinel errors and no
partial map on any failure: stdout must be a string (missing key, nil,
or any non-string type answers a fixed type error instead of the
pinned KeyError/AttributeError), input bytes ≤ 64 KiB (checked before
UTF-8 validation), stdout must be valid UTF-8, at most 1024 scanned
lines (the budget applies to lines the scan actually reaches; the
pinned `enabled: false` break short-circuits first, matching the
pinned short-circuit behavior on a 5001-line vector the oracle
confirms), each retained field value ≤ 4096 bytes, and a defensive
≤ 4 retained fields guard. Only synthetic stdout is ever parsed; no
credential/account/host data and no provider call exists in the helper
or its tests.

##### 2026-09-29 current status (R10.3b dnsutil hosts mutation; external CI pending)

R10.3b completes the dnsutil mutation surface of the pinned
`salt/modules/dnsutil.py`: `hosts_append` and `hosts_remove` are
registered (10 of the 11 public catalog functions; only `serial`
stays pending — persistent grains store). The mutation pair runs
exclusively over a new optional bounded atomic read-modify-publish
capability of `Runtime.FS` (`runtime.UpdateFileBounded`,
`internal/runtime`): implemented by `OSFileSystem` and `MemoryFS`
only, never widening the base `FileSystem` interface, with a fixed
value-free unavailable error and no `ReadFile`/`WriteFile` fallback
when the capability is absent (asserted with an interface-embedding
fake). This is a trusted same-principal local mutation API: the
caller-selected path is a PRIVILEGED input — beyond the no-follow
walk, the ORIGINAL-path validation, and the documented bounds there is
no confinement or authorization (the pinned source performs none
either); `hosts_append` may create the target (0644, exactly like the
pinned `fopen(..., "a")`) while `hosts_remove` requires an existing
file; and publication REPLACES the inode — the ordinary permission
bits are preserved, but owner and group are NOT (the staged file is
created by the calling process) and ACLs, extended attributes,
security labels, and hard links do not carry over.

The ORIGINAL caller path is validated at the dispatcher and inside
both implementations BEFORE any filesystem or map access
(R103B-SEC-01): empty paths, NUL bytes, paths over 4096 bytes, any
`..` component rejected outright (no lexical cancellation — the
symlink-then-`..`, missing-then-`..`, and non-dir-then-`..` vectors
never reach resolution), and trailing-slash or terminal `/.`
directory syntax for a file target; counting filesystems prove the
rejections happen with zero update dispatches. The OS implementation
then follows the `bounded_unix.go` descriptor-relative no-follow
discipline (every parent opened `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`, the final
component `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, regular-file check, bounded read
of at most the caller's ceiling plus one sentinel), renders and
validates the COMPLETE replacement inside a pure transform before
anything is staged, and answers every transform error at the
capability boundary with the fixed CAUSE-FREE `ErrUpdateTransform`
sentinel — constant value-free text, NO `Unwrap`, and NO custom `Is`:
the boundary never inspects the callback error at all (no `Error`,
`Is`, `As`, or `Unwrap` call, not even for classification), so no
callback text, identity chain, or attached value can escape and
`errors.Is` matches ONLY the fixed sentinel identity — a callback
error can never make the boundary classify `context.Canceled`, a
module sentinel, or any arbitrary target, and `errors.As` has no
chain to walk (R103B-SEC-06 closed: malicious-callback regressions at
the direct runtime surfaces — `Error`/`Is`/`As`/`Unwrap`/`Formatter`/
`GoString` all counting invocations and panicking — prove zero method
invocations, fixed text under `%v`/`%+v`/`%#v`/`%s`, no arbitrary
sentinel fabrication, and no payload extraction; callbacks must not
embed secrets). Real context cancellation/deadline is detected
exclusively by the runtime's independent ctx checks before and after
the transform, never by a callback-supplied error. Every injected
stage-hook/fault-seam error (the OS staging,
revalidate, and publish seams and the MemoryFS start/commit seams) is
DROPPED without invoking any fault method and answered by the fixed
cause-free `ErrUpdateStageHook`
sentinel (R103B-REGATE-01: no fault text, identity, `Unwrap`,
`errors.As`, formatting, or `errors.Is` classification; the
publish-stage hook stays a pre-publication abort — with a failing
staging cleanup it answers `ErrUpdateCleanupFailed` and it is never
the residue or durability classes). The replacement is staged in the
target directory
(`O_CREATE|O_EXCL`, 0600, short-write handling, contents+metadata
fsync), the existing ordinary permission bits are preserved (0644 for
a new file), the target identity is revalidated, and publication is
one atomic namespace operation — rename over the revalidated existing
target, or an atomic no-replace link publication for an initially
absent target on the platforms with the atomic primitive (linux plus
the linkat unix list darwin/dragonfly/freebsd/netbsd/openbsd).
Solaris creation FAILS CLOSED (R103B-GATE-01/R103B-SEC-01): the
streaming O_EXCL final form was removed because it published the name
before its contents completed, so absent-target publication answers
the fixed `ErrUpdateCreateUnsupported` error before anything is
staged, while the genuinely-atomic existing-target rename path
remains (the `GOOS=solaris` compile gate pins the fail-closed build).

Cleanup is a checked contract with distinct fixed outcomes
(R103B-GATE-03/R103B-SEC-07) — never an unconditional-cleanup claim:
a pre-publication failure with successful cleanup leaves the target
byte-identical answering the original error class; a pre-publication
failure whose staging unlink also fails answers the distinct
value-free `ErrUpdateCleanupFailed` sentinel with the target still
unchanged; and a post-publication staging-unlink failure on the
no-replace path answers the distinct `ErrUpdateStagingResidue`
sentinel with the new content live — never described as a rollback
and distinct from the committed-uncertain durability class
(post-publication parent-directory fsync failure →
`runtime: update committed but durability uncertain`). All three
outcomes are wired through unlink-failure seams in the tests.
Cancellation is checked before staging, before publication, and —
MemoryFS — after the transform and commit hook immediately before the
node replacement (R103B-GATE-02/R103B-SEC-03: a deterministic
transform-cancels-context regression asserts unchanged contents AND
metadata). Documented concurrency ceiling (R103B-SEC-04): identity
revalidation detects inode REPLACEMENT only — same-inode in-place
writes are invisible, so lost updates are possible throughout
read-transform-stage-publish and the capability is not a CAS; the
MemoryFS transaction is mutex-serialized (the next transform always
sees the committed state), which differs from the OS
last-writer-wins window; the upgrade path is cooperative
caller-held serialization.

Exact pinned semantics are ported verbatim (oracle-verified family):
`hosts_append` keeps `entries.split(',')` with no trimming and
empties preserved, the existing content parsed through the R10.3a
`parse_hosts` loop, the pinned alias filtering INCLUDING the
list-mutation-during-iteration skipping quirk (entries `[a,a]`
against an existing `a` leave one `a` to append; entries `[a,b]` with
both present never examine `b` because the first removal shrank the
list past the iterator — deliberately not "fixed" to a clean filter),
no dedup of new aliases, a `None` ip_addr rendering the literal
`None` through Python `str.format` while never matching a dict key
(even a file line whose first token is the literal `None`), the
always-prefix-LF never-terminal-LF append line (a file with a
terminal LF gains the pinned blank separator line; an empty or
missing file gains the leading blank line), and the exact pinned
result strings. `hosts_remove` keeps the full read before the split,
alias-only removal via membership in `comps[1:]` with
`comps.remove` taking the FIRST occurrence in the whole token list
(the address==alias edge removes the address token and drops the
line), one occurrence per requested entry, the >1-token survival rule
rejoined with single spaces plus LF, verbatim blank lines and
whitespace-prefixed comment lines, the dropping of pre-existing
address-only and whitespace-only lines even without a match, the
Python splitlines() boundaries, and the Python `None` success mapped
to Go nil (the CLI transports it as JSON `null`). `hosts_remove` also
keeps the pinned source ORDER: the bounded file read precedes every
entries diagnosis — the `fopen(..., "r")` IOError on a missing file
answers before the `entries.split(",")` AttributeError position, so
missing file + nil entries answers the fixed file-read class, never an
argument class — while the path safety/size bounds intentionally still
precede the file open (they read no file bytes); the entries presence
check, argument bounds, and semantic split run INSIDE the pure
transform after the snapshot is read and before anything is staged or
published, and `entries=None` stays DISTINCT from the empty string (an
empty string splits to `[""]` and keeps the pinned normal-rewrite
semantics). Because the capability boundary is now fully cause-free,
the module recognizes its own transform classifications (the no-op
sentinel, the parser ceilings, the argument class) through the
transform's captured fixed sentinel — direct comparison against
module-created sentinels, never `errors.Is` on the capability error.

Safe divergences (documented in the R10 report and here): fail-closed
read errors with the fixed value-free `dnsutil: hosts update failed`
instead of Salt's accidental write-after-read-error file creation
(`hosts_append`) and the raw IOError (`hosts_remove`); atomic
publication instead of append(2)/in-place truncate; path safety and
size bounds BEFORE any filesystem access (4096-byte hostsfile cap
proven by a counting filesystem with zero update dispatches), with the
entries bounds of `hosts_remove` intentionally following the file read
(exactly the pinned IOError-precedes-AttributeError order; the
`hosts_append` bounds stay pre-FS because the pinned append splits
entries before reading) and NUL/line-break bytes rejected value-free
(`dnsutil: invalid argument`, the same
class mapping the pinned `entries=None` AttributeError crash; the
4096-byte ip_addr cap and the 1 MiB entries cap stay); and
the inherited R10.3a parser ceilings on the `hosts_append` parse of
the existing file (`hosts_remove` keeps the pinned raw splitlines
rewrite under the same 1 MiB read ceiling). Every error surface of
the pair is value-free; the only path-echoing outputs are the two
pinned success/no-op result strings.

##### 2026-09-28 current status (R10.3a dnsutil bounded slice; external CI pending)

R10.3a registers the bounded dnsutil slice of the pinned
`salt/modules/dnsutil.py` — exactly eight of the eleven public catalog
functions (`parse_hosts`, `parse_zone`, `check_ip`, `A`, `AAAA`, `NS`,
`SPF`, `MX`) as one Go family (`modules/exec/dnsutil`) with the two
private helpers of the pinned source kept private (`_to_seconds` backs
the SOA fields of `parse_zone`; `_has_dig` backs the delegation gate).
The frozen 2026-08-29 PTD-EXEC rows for these eight names are
superseded: they are registered. Three public functions stay pending
with specific reasons and upgrade paths (no 100%-or-family-complete
claim is made for dnsutil): `hosts_append` and `hosts_remove` because
the pinned implementations mutate arbitrary caller-supplied file paths
with no validation, backup, or atomicity — upgrade path: a bounded
regular/no-follow writer over the same `Runtime.FS`/`ReadFileBounded`
discipline this slice uses (validated destination, temp-file rename),
following the hosts module's fixture-root override precedent — and
`serial` because its pinned contract requires a persistent grains
store (`dnsserial_<zone>` across runs; `update=True` must increment
the stored value) that StateKit does not yet have — upgrade path:
register once a persistent local grains/state store module lands. The
generated R10 report (`docs/differential/R10/report.yaml`,
`round: R10.3a`) records 13 dnsutil catalog functions, 11 public, 8
registered, 3 pending (hosts_append, hosts_remove, serial); R10 totals
30 catalog / 26 public / 23 registered / 3 pending plus the unchanged
7 dig aliases, mock-only; the R3-R9 report hashes are unchanged. The
catalog regeneration that accompanies this phase
(`go run ./tools/salt-reference`) moves the dnsutil family into
`implemented_families` and records the eight new names in
`docs/catalog/coverage.yaml` (source inventory 1240→1248, catalog
intersection 1211→1219; `compatibility.yaml` implemented 117→118,
excluded 50→49); the dnsutil catalog file itself is unchanged.

Parsing surface: `parse_hosts` and `parse_zone` read files only
through `runtime.ReadFileBounded` over `Runtime.FS` with an explicit
1 MiB ceiling per read — a fixed divergence from the pinned unbounded
`salt.utils.files.fopen` — and the bounded read requires a regular
file and never follows symlinks (final component or any parent), so
devices, FIFOs, and symlink-redirected paths are rejected before any
content is allocated. The boundary is for local trusted
same-principal CLI use only, and every error surface is value-free
(no file content and no caller path travels in a result, error, or
log; no test reads the host `/etc/hosts` — MemoryFS fixtures only).
`parse_hosts` keeps the pinned shapes exactly: Python-falsy inline
input (None or the empty string) triggers the file read, a failed
read answers the exact pinned result string
`Error: hosts data was not found`, comments are recognized only when
`#` is the first character of the line (an inline `#` becomes an
ordinary alias token; a ` # col0` line contributes the `#` IP key),
duplicate aliases accumulate per IP in encounter order with
duplicates kept, a bare-IP line answers an allocated non-nil empty
alias list (JSON `[]`, never `null`), and the default path is exactly
`/etc/hosts`. Python `splitlines()`/`split()` whitespace semantics
are ported exactly (`\r`, `\r\n`, `\v`, `\f`, U+001C..U+001E, U+0085,
U+2028, U+2029 boundaries; U+001F a `split()` separator but not a
line boundary — the dig family's verified predicate family). One
documented safe divergence: a whitespace-only line raises IndexError
in the pinned source and is skipped here. `parse_zone` ports the
pinned simplistic line parser (semicolon stripping, `$DIRECTIVE`
capture, the `(`…`)` multi-line SOA join including the
unterminated-parenthesis partial-result quirk, the global `@`→ORIGIN
replacement, substring SOA detection, the `comps.pop(1)` branch for
non-IN second tokens, CONTACT's first-dot→`@` replacement, the NS
list, the first-MX-only quirk, the A/AAAA TARGET/TTL form for
owner-TTL-IN records beside the generic string bucket for 4-token
records, and TXT/CAA/PTR through the generic bucket) — the parser
ceiling matches the pinned source (not RFC 1035 complete: no
$INCLUDE, no escape/quoting, no TTL inheritance), Python dict
insertion order is not preserved by Go maps (list order is), and
every pinned crash position (short NS/PTR/MX lines, a record before
any ORIGIN, a directive without a value, a non-numeric H/D time
value, and directive/record type collisions over the NS/A/TXT keys)
maps to one fixed value-free malformed-zone error with no partial
results. A truthy `zonefile` is read first through the bounded read
and its content replaces the inline zone on success (an empty file
answers the pinned `Error: Zone data was not found` even when inline
data exists — oracle-verified), while read failures silently keep
the inline data exactly like the pinned `try/except pass`. Every
expected parse shape was oracle-verified by executing the pinned
Python source locally (the pinned
`tests/pytests/unit/modules/test_dnsutil.py` fixture included).

`_to_seconds` (private) keeps the pinned quirks exactly: the pinned
unit vectors (`4H`→14400, `1D`→86400, `2W`→604800, `""`→604800,
`604801`→604800), case-insensitive H/D/W, every `H`/`D` removed
before the parse, the W branch answering one week without any numeric
parse (`w`, `abcW`), the else branch answering one week for
unparsable values (`abc`, U+001C-wrapped digits), zero and negatives
passing through (`0H`→0, `-2H`→-7200, `-1`→-1), `168H` landing
exactly on the cap, and Python base-10 `int()` grammar — outer
int() whitespace (` 12 H `→43200), Unicode Nd digits
(`２４H`→86400, `٢٤H`→86400), single between-digit underscores
(`2_4H`→86400; `_24H` rejects like the pinned ValueError crash
position), and one ASCII sign (`+2H`→7200). Two documented
micro-divergences: magnitudes beyond int64 saturate (positive
saturation still caps to one week; negative saturation answers
`math.MinInt64` where Python keeps the exact arbitrary-precision
negative), and Go's simple ToUpper does not reproduce the single
U+1E96 full-uppercase expansion (Python takes the H branch there and
crashes; StateKit answers the else branch's one week).

Delegation surface: `check_ip`, `A`, `AAAA`, `NS`, `SPF`, and `MX`
delegate to the registered dig family through `rt.Exec.Call` — the
StateKit nested-invocation boundary (the caller's context carries
cancellation and deadlines into the nested call; the dig module's own
trusted-process boundary, budgets, and call-time gates apply per
delegation) — with exact argument pass-through: nameservers forward
as-is, `NS` forwards `resolve` with the pinned `True` default, `SPF`
forwards `record` with the pinned exact `"SPF"` default, `MX`
forwards `resolve` with the pinned `False` default, and the delegated
value and error class propagate unchanged. dnsutil never parses
addresses itself and never dispatches a process: no `netip`, no
`net.DefaultResolver`, no `net.LookupIP`, and no socket use exist
anywhere in the family. `_has_dig` is ported as the
trusted-resolution gate through the Runner's optional
`process.TrustedCommandResolver` capability (the dig module's
documented PATH `which()` divergence), so a failing resolver, a
capability-less Runner, or no Runner at all answers the pinned result
string `This function requires dig, which is not currently
available` with zero dispatch; the pinned A/AAAA
`socket.getaddrinfo` fallback when dig is unavailable is an
explicitly deferred divergence (no host-resolver egress). When the
gate passes but the registry carries no matching dig function — the
pinned `__salt__` lookup crash position — the call fails closed with
one fixed value-free unavailable error.

Evidence: direct/registry/CLI tests carry the pinned
`tests/pytests/unit/modules/test_dnsutil.py` vectors and the
oracle-verified parse shapes; the dig delegation is pinned at direct,
registry, and CLI surfaces over the real dig family with a scripted
fake Runner behind a test trusted resolver (exact fixed argv
`-r +short -q <name> -t <type>` plus one validated `@server`, exact
child environment allowlist, shell-free); the dnsutil behavioral
tests carry the `dns_contract` build tag so the default host CI
`go test ./...` does not execute them, and the tag boundary is
statically pinned by `TestR10DNSContractTagBoundary` (now covering
both the three dig and the four dnsutil contract test names). No dig
binary is executed, no DNS name is resolved, no network is touched,
and no host `/etc/hosts` or zone file is read by any test.

Remediation (2026-09-28, within the R10.3a phase committed as `b09faf6`):
the final review findings R103A-FINAL-01 and R10.3A-SEC-01 are closed in
`modules/exec/dnsutil`, and the security-gate follow-up
R103A-GATE-01/R103A-GATE-02/R103A-SEC-FINAL-01 tightened the result
budgets to the retained serialized output. R103A-FINAL-01: a
multi-line `(`…`)` continuation join that strips every token (the
whitespace-only join of the multiline zone `"(\n)\n"` — an empty token
slice after the parenthesis/continuation parsing) reached `comps[0]`
and panicked; the pinned parser raises IndexError in the same position,
and the port answers the exact fixed value-free `dnsutil: malformed
zone data` error with no partial result and no panic, pinned at
direct, registry, and CLI surfaces with zero dig dispatch.
R10.3A-SEC-01/R103A-GATE-01/02 (exact ceilings, all enforced before or
during parsing with one fixed value-free error per class —
`dnsutil: input exceeds limit` for the source-byte ceilings,
`dnsutil: parser limit exceeded` for the input-record and cell
ceilings, `dnsutil: result byte limit exceeded` for the serialized
result representation, `dnsutil: result item limit exceeded` for the
retained result items — and no partial results): inline `hosts`/`zone`
values are capped at the shared 1 MiB ceiling of the `ReadFileBounded`
file reads before any processing (exactly 1 MiB parses; one byte over
rejects); `hostsfile`/`zonefile` path arguments over 4096 bytes are
rejected before the filesystem is touched and answer the pinned
read-failure compatibility shapes; parsing is bounded at at most 4096
input records (non-blank, non-comment lines), 4096 bytes per parsed
token or derived cell, 8192 retained result items — every retained
JSON object member across all nested maps plus every list element and
duplicate-appended element, so one owner-TTL-IN-A record accounts its
owner member and the TARGET and TTL members it inserts — and 4 MiB of
the COMPLETE serialized result representation: every map key
(including every expanded `'@'`→ORIGIN generic-bucket key), every
value, the exact `encoding/json` escaping (quotes, backslash, the
`\b\f\n\r\t` short forms, the remaining control bytes, the HTML
triplet, U+2028/U+2029, and invalid UTF-8), and every nested
map/array delimiter, colon, and comma. The result budgets are tracked
exactly as the retained output while it is built — a `jsonStringLength`
length oracle plus per-insertion structural deltas, never a
`json.Marshal` of the result and never a counting walker that buffers
the encoding — with overflow-safe counters, and each `reserve` runs
BEFORE the key/value/row is inserted, so a map-key overwrite replaces
the previous value's bytes per the retained output (monotonic: no
sequence of records, overwrites, or duplicate appends can end over a
ceiling the counter did not see) while duplicate rows keep Salt
order. The `'@'`→ORIGIN expansion is guarded before allocation by the
exact int64 match-count estimate `len(line)+matches*(len(origin)-1)`
against the 1 MiB ceiling; the multi-line join and the expansion are
linear builders; and every slice/index access is length-checked.
Boundaries are pinned by tests with small inputs: a fake bounded
filesystem reporting oversize, a counting fake filesystem proving the
too-long path never reaches `Runtime.FS`, the inline length cap at
exactly 1 MiB, repeated `@` plus a 4096-byte origin at 255/256 matches
(1,044,734 bytes parse / 1,048,831 reject), hosts rows at 4096/4097,
the malformed empty continuation, and the result-budget gate probes —
the ~17 KiB zone (origin = 3999 `a` chars + dot, 1024 distinct records
`x. IN @<i> @`) that previously answered ~8.2 MB of JSON rejects with
the fixed byte error and nil result (the exact boundary located by
bisection against an `encoding/json` test-oracle map: the largest
fitting record count parses with byte-exact oracle shape and size, one
more rejects), 1100 distinct `t<i>@` type keys over a 4081-byte origin
reject before the expanded bucket key is inserted, 4095 unique
owner-TTL-IN-A rows retain 12,287 nested items and reject with the
fixed item error (exact boundary 2730 rows = 8192 items), control-byte
escaping amplification on parse_hosts (each 4096-byte `\x01` alias
retains 24,578 JSON bytes) rejects value-free, and under-ceiling
distinct buckets carrying quotes/backslash/control/DEL/HTML-triplet/
non-ASCII keys and values parse successfully with the measured
`encoding/json` size within the cap (U+2028/U+2029 are
pythonSplitlines line boundaries that cannot survive into a parser
cell, so their escaping classes are oracle-pinned at the string level)
— each rejecting with no partial map or slice, and the module contract
and CLI surfaces preserve the nil results and value-free errors with
zero dig dispatch. Registration is unchanged: R10.3a stays
exactly 8 of the 11 public dnsutil catalog functions registered, with

replacements: a plain-string bucket owner rewritten by the
owner-TTL-IN-A form gained the TARGET and TTL members but reserved an
item delta of zero, an object flattened back to a string (and a
top-level bucket or NS/MX list flattened by a directive) never
returned its removed descendants, so the item counter drifted off the
retained output in both directions. The budget now caches every
top-level member's whole retained subtree item count beside its byte
size and reserves the exact new-minus-old delta of BOTH budgets on
every replacement (a per-entry subtree oracle answers 2 items for the
TARGET/TTL object and 0 for the scalar), positive deltas before
insertion and negative deltas applied only on the successful
replacement path — Salt overwrite and duplicate-append order
semantics untouched. Boundary regressions are independently computed:
the gate vector ($ORIGIN + two generic A strings for x0/x1 + the two
owner-TTL-IN-A rewrites of those owners + 2729 fresh
owner-TTL-IN-A rows) retains 8195 final items and now rejects with
`dnsutil: result item limit exceeded` and a nil result (the pre-fix
counter read 8191 and let the 8195-item result escape), the separate
2730-row structure retains exactly 8192 items and still parses, the
top-level bucket→directive shrink (101-item TXT subtree → 1) admits
the exact-8192 fill the stale counter falsely rejected, and the nested
object→scalar rewrite returns its two items at the same boundary.
R103A-FINAL-BYTES-01 — the nested TARGET/TTL object contributes
exactly 18 structural bytes excluding the encoded values
(`{`, `"TARGET"`, `:`, `,`, `"TTL"`, `:`, `}`), not 19; both

pins a nested A/AAAA result whose exact compact encoding is exactly
4,194,304 bytes (accepted, byte-exact shape, escape classes and every
map-member delimiter included) with one encoded byte above rejected
before insertion and a nil result. All four ceilings (1 MiB
input/expansion, 4096 records/cells, 8192 items, 4 MiB complete
result) are unchanged, the counters stay overflow-safe, the parser
never marshals the result to measure it, and registration, pending
ledger, and external CI status are unchanged.

##### 2026-09-28 current status (R10.2 dig exec family; R10.2 remediation closed; external CI pending)

R10.2 registers the complete dig exec family of the pinned
`salt/modules/dig.py` — the nine canonical public functions `check_ip`,
`A`, `PTR`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `NS`, `SPF`, `MX`, `TXT` plus the seven
source aliases of the pinned module tail (`a`, `ptr`, `aaaa`, `cname`,
`ns`, `spf`, `mx`; the pinned source defines no `txt` alias) — as one Go
family (`modules/exec/dig`) over the central shell-free Runner. The
frozen 2026-08-29 PTD-EXEC rows for the dig family are superseded for
these names: they are registered. The generated R10 report
(`docs/differential/R10/report.yaml`, `round: R10.2`) records 9 dig
catalog functions, 9 public, 9/9 registered, 7/7 source aliases (reported
separately from the canonical totals), R10 totals 17 catalog / 15 public /
15 registered canonical plus 7 registered aliases, mock-only; the R3-R9
report hashes are unchanged. The catalog regeneration that accompanies
this phase (`go run ./tools/salt-reference`) moves the dig family into
`implemented_families` and records the sixteen new names in
`docs/catalog/coverage.yaml` (source inventory 1224→1240, catalog
intersection 1202→1211 for the nine canonical registrations); the dig
catalog file itself keeps exactly the nine canonical functions.

Source and transport: `dig.__virtual__` gates the whole module on the dig
binary — StateKit registers the family statically (an architectural
constraint, documented exactly: the registration inventory and the
differential report must stay environment-independent while the
dns_contract evidence containers ship no dig binary, so bootstrap cannot
skip the family without making the cataloged surface host-dependent) and
enforces the gate per call through the Runner's optional
`process.TrustedCommandResolver` capability (when trusted resolution
fails, every `dig.*` function including `check_ip` fails closed with a
fixed value-free error and zero dispatch; a Runner without the
capability cannot verify the executable, so every `dig.*` function
including `check_ip` fails closed with the fixed value-free
unverified-executable error and zero dispatch — the module never
performs a host LookPath of its own and never substitutes a bare-name
PATH dispatch). Every dispatch is the fixed dig
command with the separate argv `-r +short -q <name> -t <type>` and an
optional single trailing validated `@server` element, always
`Shell=false`, with no generic flags and no shell; PTR validates its
argument as a bare IP literal and always queries the fixed reverse form
(`d.c.b.a.in-addr.arpa` or the nibble-reversed `ip6.arpa` name) instead
of the pinned raw `-x <host>` spelling, so no caller-controlled dig flag
surface exists.

Trusted native process boundary (R102-SEC-01, closed with full
symlink-chain verification): the pinned module
launches a PATH-resolved dig and inherits the full minion environment;
StateKit never launches a PATH-resolved dig. `DefaultRunner` implements
`process.TrustedCommandResolver` narrowly — only the fixed `dig` name,
only the fixed canonical system candidate paths (`/usr/bin/dig`,
`/bin/dig`, and `/usr/local/bin/dig`) — and resolves each candidate by
walking every component of the candidate and of every symlink target
with `Lstat`: every directory on the chain must be root-owned with no
group/world write, every symlink must be root-owned (Linux symlinks are
always `lrwxrwxrwx`, so the enforceable link controls are its owner and
the non-group/world-writable, root-owned containing directory),
relative symlink targets join the link's directory and absolute symlink
targets are cleaned, and every resulting normalized absolute path must
stay inside the approved system roots (`/bin`, `/usr`, `/usr/local`) —
containment is decided on the normalized target, never a raw lexical
prefix (R102-FINAL-02: `/usr/../opt/vendor/dig` normalizes to
`/opt/vendor/dig` and is rejected unless the cleaned final target
remains inside a canonical approved root), symlink hops are bounded so
loops and deep chains fail closed, and the final target must be an
absolute regular
executable that is root-owned with no group/world write; unsupported
names and platforms fail closed with `ErrTrustedCommandUnsupported` and
missing or untrusted binaries with `ErrTrustedCommandUnavailable` (the
non-unix build carries the fail-closed stub and its own build-tagged
tests). The exact remaining native runtime requirement: a user-installed
dig outside the canonical candidates and approved roots — a homebrew or
`$HOME` prefix, any custom `PATH` directory — is unsupported; resolution
fails closed with the fixed unavailable error and the operator remedy is
installing dig under a canonical candidate path owned by root in
non-group/world-writable directories. The resolved absolute path
becomes argv[0] of every dig dispatch (a resolver answering a relative or
empty path fails closed), and the child environment is exactly the fixed
allowlist `HOME=/nonexistent` (a fixed nonexistent directory; `-r` is
kept and already ignores per-user digrc), `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`,
`LANG=C`, `LC_ALL=C`,
`TZ=UTC` — nothing is inherited, so `RES_OPTIONS`, `LOCALDOMAIN`,
`HOSTALIASES`, `LD_*`, and caller secrets cannot reach the dig process.
A Runner without the resolver capability cannot verify the executable:
every `dig.*` function fails closed with the fixed value-free
unverified-executable error and zero dispatch, and no LookPath or
bare-name PATH fallback exists anywhere. The resolver's filesystem walk
is unit-tested
over a synthetic stat/symlink seam (positive resolution, symlink chains
inside the approved roots, candidate order, non-root owner, group/world-
writable binary and every ancestor including the filesystem root,
non-regular, non-executable, missing, dangling, and looped candidates,
user-owned symlink, symlink target outside the approved roots, relative
traversal escape, the dig-only name allowlist) plus synthetic temp
trees driven through the production `Lstat`/`Readlink` walker (safe
root chain/link, user-owned symlink, writable parent, loop, traversal,
absolute dot-dot targets that lexically start inside the approved root
but clean outside it — final-component and mid-chain directory
symlinks, with the safe root-internal absolute pass retained,
R102-FINAL-02 — candidate outside allowed roots; only ownership is
synthesized because the unprivileged test cannot `chown(2)` to root)
so no test depends on — or executes — a native dig binary; the sole
real-filesystem vector only stats.

Limits (fixed, documented divergences from the pinned module, which has
none): one shared 10s operation deadline per public call, at most 2s (or
the remaining deadline) per dig process, at most 10 dig processes per
operation (the SPF→TXT fallback and the NS/MX child A lookups are
counted), at most 5 simultaneously active lookups, at most 64 KiB stdout
and 8 KiB stderr captured per process, at most 256 KiB aggregate captured
output, and at most 256 result entries; recursion carries active-path
cycle detection keyed by (query, type, resolver) with no sibling
deduplication (two includes of one target both dispatch, matching the
pinned source), and truncation, cancellation, deadline, launch, and
budget failures reject the whole operation without partial results.

Input validation is fail-closed before any dispatch (a security
divergence from the pinned source, which passes caller strings to dig
unvalidated): query names are bounded ASCII DNS names (1..63-byte labels,
at most 253 bytes excluding one terminal dot, underscore labels
supported) rejecting empty names, empty interior labels, whitespace,
control and NUL bytes, escaped and other non-allowlisted bytes,
option-like (leading `-`) and server-like (leading `@`) forms, over-long
labels and names, and non-ASCII; nameservers are absent, a validated
hostname, or a bare IPv4/IPv6 literal — never an @-prefixed,
port-bearing, URL, CIDR, bracketed, or zoned form; the SPF record
argument accepts exactly `SPF` or `TXT`; and every response-derived NS
host, MX exchange, and SPF include/redirect target is revalidated
through the same validators before its child dispatch.

Verified Python semantics (R102-F2/R102-F3, corrected against the runtime
checker): `check_ip` keeps the IPv4 1..32 and IPv6 8..128 prefix ranges
without host-bit alignment; the address half follows Python
`ipaddress.ip_address` over `net/netip` — leading-zero octets, short v4
forms, whitespace-wrapped literals, and zoned IPv4 literals are invalid,
while the scoped IPv6 literal `fe80::1%eth0` is valid (Python ≥ 3.9
`IPv6Address` accepts scope ids; the zone never reaches the fixed PTR
reverse name) and a v4-in-v6 textual literal reports IPv6; the prefix
`int()` accepts the Python base-10 grammar — outer int() whitespace
(the ASCII whitespace set plus non-ASCII Python spaces such as U+3000,
but NOT U+001C..U+001F: `int('\x1c24\x1f')` raises ValueError even
though `chr(0x1c).isspace()` is true, so the int() predicate is a
distinct `pythonIntWhitespace` that excludes the four ASCII information
separators), one ASCII
`+`/`-` sign, Unicode Nd decimal digits (`192.0.2.1/２４` and `/٢٤`
parse as 24), and single underscores strictly between digits
(`192.0.2.1/2_4` parses; `_24`, `24_`, `2__4`, `+_24`, and interior
non-digits fail like ValueError), with oversized magnitudes failing the
range check like Python's large ints. The Python whitespace predicate
(`str.isspace()`/`str.split()`/`str.rstrip()`: Go's `unicode.IsSpace`
plus U+001C..U+001F, which CPython's Latin-1 whitespace table classifies
as space and Go does not) drives the trailing rstrip applied once to dig
stdout and the whitespace token split used for MX rows and SPF sections,
so a trailing U+001C run is trimmed from TXT and raw NS output while
interior U+001C survives the newline split and `10\x1cmx.example.` is
the two-field MX row `[10 mx.example.]`; the split answers allocated
non-nil empty slices for every empty-token row exactly like Python's
`line.split()` (a Python list is never null), so an empty successful MX
stdout is `[[]]` and an interior blank/whitespace row is `[]` — JSON
`[]`, never `null` (R102-FINAL-01) — and response bytes and string
limits are unchanged.

Preserved quirks: A and AAAA share one predicate (the verified check_ip
above, so scoped IPv6 literals are retained like Python) and retain
cross-family literals, CIDR strings, order, and duplicates; PTR and TXT
keep the literal newline split retaining empties, quotes, and trailing
dots (an empty successful stdout answers `[""]` like the pinned split,
and raw MX answers `[[]]` whose rows are allocated non-nil slices
exactly like Salt's `line.split()`, so the JSON shape is `[]` — never
`null` — for every empty row); CNAME answers the stdout string on success
including empty and `[]` on a completed nonzero exit; NS defaults to
resolve=true and raw-splits when false; MX takes only the first A address
when resolving; SPF falls back to TXT only on an exactly empty answer
with record exactly SPF (counted against the call budget), strips every
double quote, requires the exact first token `v=spf1`, honors `redirect=`
only as the second token, and keeps the pinned include/ip4/ip6 regex with
ordering and duplicates. The pinned crash positions map to fixed results
instead of panics: a lone `v=spf1` answers `[]`, a malformed MX row under
resolve=true and an MX exchange whose A lookup answers no address are
rejected as malformed aggregates value-free, and a nonzero dig process
exit maps to the source empty fallback wherever the pinned function
specifies one, while Runner launch/deadline/cancellation/truncation
failures stay fixed value-free errors that carry no raw argv, stdout,
stderr, domain, or resolver bytes.

The 20 configured cases cover `psql_query` only, not live validation of the
other 49 PostgreSQL public functions. They include both `write=false`
INSERT RETURNING with native persistence observation and `write=true` UPDATE
RETURNING with native committed read-back; these are configured assertions,
not observations from an external run.

The arbitrary SQL entry point is privileged, not a safe read API: `write=false`
does **not** enforce read-only access (data-modifying CTEs/functions inside
COPY can persist writes). A timeout, client/Runner error, or result-limit
failure returns no partial result but cannot establish whether a prior write
committed; callers must reconcile an unknown write outcome before retrying.
COPY CSV compatibility maps SQL NULL and the empty string to the same empty
string in the returned string map; callers needing lossless values require a
separately proven transport. The bounded lexical/size restrictions and mock
coverage are documented in the generated report, whose external status remains
`pending_external_ci`. No live PostgreSQL is run by this documentation update.

files and workflow are ready for the required live gate for the already-ported
MySQL read-only/catalog/plugin subset, while preserving the existing fake-Runner
contract boundary for unit, registry, and CLI tests. The local mock/static gate
passed 13 orchestration tests, relevant Go tests, `go vet`, shell syntax, and
workflow YAML validation. Live MySQL GitHub execution remains
`pending_external_ci`; no live 14/14 result is recorded here. The user will
validate the external run after synchronization.

| Phase | Scope | Implementation executor role | Independent gate(s) | Result / boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `E5.1` | Disposable official MySQL 8.4 service, production `statekit` binary, native `mysql` client, 14 bounded live cases, value-free report, and reusable orchestration under `tests/live/mysql/` | `devops-platform-engineer-senior` | `backend-engineer-lead` + `security-engineer-senior` — both requested changes on the local sandbox/trust boundary; neither is an approval | implementation files/workflow ready; local mock/static gate passed; status `pending_external_ci`; live evidence is limited to `mysql.version`, `db_list`, `db_exists`, `plugins_list`, and `plugin_status` plus authenticated readiness, negative auth/connection checks, and native postconditions; no live 14/14, full R9 live coverage, or differential parity is claimed |

The E5.1 workflow is intended to use the Docker Hub manifest reference pinned by digest
`mysql:8.4@sha256:85b9bf2e29cf836ecb8c2a15a935d4ba0c606631dff1dd79531a11983c638f2a`;
the external CI run must check that digest after pull. The workflow is also
intended to use
immutable full-commit action references, `contents: read` only, and
`persist-credentials: false`. Its first runtime action must be a fail-closed
host/rootless/remote/isolation preflight; it must use `pull_request` rather than
`pull_request_target`, an internal private service network, an ephemeral client
image instead of a host-path mount, no host socket, device, host port, or
privileged mode, and explicit cleanup on success, failure, and cancellation.
These are workflow intent and CI-enforced checks pending the external run. The
only accepted runtime is local rootless Podman. The server is intended to run
with the pinned image's explicit `999:999` non-root identity and no added
capabilities; client containers must use explicit `65532:65532` identity with all
capabilities dropped. The created-container policy must be inspected before start
using only allowlisted direct format fields; exact no-new-privileges,
exclusive-network, user, capability, device, bind, socket, secret, and tmpfs
conditions must fail closed rather than gaining a capability exception.
On external CI, credentials must be generated at runtime and created from stdin
as Podman secrets.
MySQL must receive only `_FILE` paths; each client must copy a defaults file to
tmpfs for one process. Credential values must not be written to repository files,
container Config.Env, argv, layers, inspect output, fixtures, reports,
artifacts, or diagnostics. Dependency fetch must be separate from the
network-denied pinned-image production build and Python checks with explicit OCI
isolation; an unverifiable hosted runner must not fall back to direct execution.
Cleanup must verify removal of owned containers, the private network, secrets,
and client image. Native negative cases must require their fixed MySQL
authentication/connection error marker; timeout, runtime, setup, cleanup, and
unrelated exits must be failures.
On external CI, the report must be fresh and successfully written, with execution and final
return codes, and incomplete, cancelled, skipped, or nonzero execution fails.
Repeated INT/TERM must be shielded during bounded TERM-then-KILL cleanup;
SIGKILL, runner loss, or host loss can prevent cleanup/report publication and
therefore cannot produce pass evidence. The native client must check the seeded database
and installed plugin independently after StateKit calls. SQLite is outside this
phase.

The committed differential report remains the mock-only R9 differential
record; E5.1 does not rewrite it or claim live parity for the remaining R9
families and functions.

##### 2026-09-21 R9.3j MySQL database lifecycle — implementation phase; external live CI pending

R9.3j is a separate backend implementation phase from E5.1. It ports only the
pinned Salt `mysql.db_create` and `mysql.db_remove` contracts into the existing
Go module, registry, and CLI surfaces. The port remains driver-free and uses
the bounded central Runner with shell-free argv, finite timeout/output limits,
MYSQL_PWD credential transport, value-free validation errors, identifier
quoting, redaction, and the source's false-on-existing/absent lifecycle
shapes. The pinned functions have no `force` parameter; no force surface is
added.

The exact evidence boundary is:

* **Local mock/static evidence (permitted and completed for this phase):**
  direct, registry, and CLI fake-Runner tests; generated R9.3j differential
  report; deterministic live-harness inventory/orchestration tests; shell
  syntax and static/workflow checks. These tests do not start MySQL and do not
  prove database behavior.
* **External live evidence (pending):** the GitHub E5.2 job must execute all
  23 inventory cases with `cases_skipped: 0`, create a unique disposable
  database, verify presence and absence independently with the native client,
  assert StateKit create/repeat/remove contracts, exercise invalid-identifier,
  authentication, and connection negatives, and perform cleanup on every exit
  path. No GitHub run success is recorded here; status is exactly
  `pending_external_ci`.
* The official MySQL 8.4 digest and existing full-commit action SHAs remain
  unchanged. SQLite is outside this phase. The committed R9 report is still a
  mock-only differential record, not live Salt parity.

Backend F2-F4 remediation by `backend-engineer-senior` records three explicit
compatibility ceilings without weakening the shared security boundary:

* A nonzero `db_exists` preflight is an unknown absence. StateKit fails closed
  before `db_create`/`CREATE`, whereas the pinned Salt `db_create` can receive
  `False`, reconnect, and attempt `CREATE` after an `OperationalError`.
* The fixed catalog uses exact client-side membership. The pinned unescaped
  `SHOW DATABASES LIKE` treats `%` and `_` as wildcard-shaped input; direct and
  CLI regression vectors preserve that difference. Mutation statements still
  use the validated quoted-identifier path rather than interpolating raw SQL.
* After a successful `DROP`, a failed/nonzero post-check is `db_exists ==
  False` compatibility data and therefore the public `db_remove` result is
  `true`; it is distinct from a failed `DROP`, which returns `false`.

The remediation adds focused direct and CLI vectors for timeout, output limits,
cancellation after preflight, phase-specific redaction, identifier/option
quoting and validation, plus the corrected public post-check result. Report
counts remain unchanged and `external_ci_status` remains
`pending_external_ci`; no live database or commit is part of this phase.

##### 2026-09-22 R9.3l MySQL `alter_db` — implementation complete; external live CI pending

R9.3l ports the pinned Salt `mysql.alter_db` contract from the locked
`mysql.py`, catalog, and unit vectors. The public function is registered as
`mysql.alter_db` and is available through the direct runtime, exec registry,
and CLI argument decoder. It obtains `character_set` and `collate` defaults
through the existing `mysql.db_get` fixed catalog before issuing one
`ALTER DATABASE` statement through the shared native CLI Runner. Explicit
non-empty options preserve the source's bare-token SQL shape; nil and empty
options preserve Salt's truthiness fallback to the catalog values. Database
identifiers use the validated, backtick-doubled path, and raw charset/collation
positions accept only value-free, identifier-like ASCII tokens.

The transport remains driver-free and shell-free: argv, stdout, stderr,
cancellation, 30-second timeout, 4 MiB output caps, MYSQL_PWD-only connection
transport, and complete phase redaction are inherited from the shared Runner.
The compatibility and safety surface is explicit: source-result vectors cover
representative truthy/falsy `cursor.execute` returns, but the native CLI cannot
expose that DB-API value or an exact affected-row predicate. StateKit therefore
maps exit zero to `true` and a server-rejected/nonzero exit to `false`; this is
the documented CLI ceiling, not a claim of exact cursor-result parity. A
successful rowless `db_get` is `{}`: two explicit non-empty options may proceed
like the source's default-bypassing expressions, while omitted/empty or partial
options fail closed when a default is absent. A nonzero `db_get` is `[]` and
never authorizes ALTER, including with two explicit options. Runner,
cancellation, output-limit, invalid-auth/connection, identifier, and option
failures remain value-free errors or the pinned catalog compatibility shape as
applicable, with no unsafe mutation after failed preflight.

The local stateful mock also performs post-alter `db_get` and fixed seed-row
readback: accepted ALTER changes only modeled charset/collation metadata,
rejected ALTER preserves the metadata, and the seed remains unchanged. This is
mock evidence; it does not replace the pending native MySQL observer.

The exact evidence boundary is:

* **Local mock/static evidence (completed in conforming rootless Podman):**
  direct source-parity vectors, registry tests, CLI mock tests, R9 report
  generation, coverage regeneration, Go test/race/vet checks, shell/Python/YAML
  checks, and deterministic live-harness orchestration checks. These checks do
  not start MySQL and do not claim live Salt parity.
* **External live evidence (pending):** the existing GitHub E5.2 workflow must
  preserve the prior 23 cases and execute 13 additional R9.3l cases (36 total,
  zero skips): reserve and create/seed a disposable database, independently
  observe defaults and explicit/default-preserving charset/collation changes
  with the native client, read back with native client and StateKit `db_get`,
  exercise invalid auth/connection/identifier/option negatives, verify the
  seeded row after each successful alter/readback, and verify cleanup. The
  native CLI can validate SQL/metadata/seed outcomes but cannot observe the
  pinned MySQLdb `cursor.execute` return predicate exactly. No local live
  MySQL is used and no GitHub run success is recorded; status is exactly
  `pending_external_ci`.
* The SQLite job and SQLite tests are outside this overlay and are not changed.

The source-compatible result ladder is explicit: an empty name returns false
without a Runner call; an already-installed plugin makes `plugin_add` true; an
absent plugin makes `plugin_remove` true; and a successful fixed

fail-closed CLI boundary for Salt's separate `_connect`/query exceptions: the

structural bytes are rejected value-free before Runner invocation. Shared
timeout, cancellation, argv/output bounds, MYSQL_PWD transport, and longest
first redaction cover the preflight and mutation phases. No plugin shared
object is bundled, downloaded, or installed by the local contract.

catalog names with exact Go string equality, including an explicit
uppercase/mixed-case compatibility vector, and that exact identity is the
StateKit contract. The pinned Salt `PLUGIN_NAME = %(name)s` equality is

##### 2026-09-23 R9.3p MySQL `query` — implementation complete; external live CI pending

R9.3p implements the pinned Salt `mysql.query(database, query, **connection_args)`
surface in the direct runtime, exec registry, and CLI decoder. Arbitrary SQL is an
explicit privileged boundary: the validated statement is bounded and sent only as
stdin to the native `mysql` client in binary/batch mode, never interpolated into
shell text or argv. Database, connection, password, and runas inputs are validated
separately; the shared finite timeout, cancellation, stdin/stdout/stderr limits,
truncation rejection, and value-free redaction/error behavior remain in force.
One SQL statement is accepted, including multiline comments and quoted semicolons;
client backslash commands and NUL/oversize input fail closed. For ordinary
non-row DDL/DML, a fixed `SELECT ROW_COUNT()` probe is appended inside the same
bounded stdin payload so the public `rows affected` shape remains useful.
R93P-01 is an explicit compatibility ceiling: because the native client
session's backslash-escape SQL mode is not proven before scanning, any
backslash inside a single-, double-, or backtick-quoted token is rejected
before framing and Runner invocation. Backslashes in comments remain allowed;
the upgrade path is a separately proven matching SQL mode, not a permissive
scanner guess. Direct, registry, and CLI no-dispatch regressions cover odd and
even backslash quote-boundary fixtures.
The pinned no-args path's `%%` to `%` normalization is applied before transport;
the caller statement receives a real delimiter before any trailing line/block
comments, so an existing terminator, quoted semicolon, or comment cannot swallow
the probe. `WITH ... SELECT` is the documented read contract, while a CTE whose
final top-level command is `UPDATE`/`INSERT`/`DELETE`/`REPLACE` is the write
contract and receives the probe. This comment-aware/CTE classification is a
tested StateKit ceiling over Salt's raw-prefix behavior. The CLI exposes only a
process exit, so query and connection nonzero exits both use value-free `false`
rather than claiming Salt's connection-only `{}` shape; canonical cancellation,
deadline, output-limit, and input-limit sentinels are preserved, and wrapped
arbitrary Runner errors collapse to a value-free execution error.

The native CLI compatibility ceiling is explicit rather than overclaimed: batch
output cannot distinguish a literal string `NULL` from SQL NULL, the probe cannot
reproduce every MySQLdb/DB-API cursor rowcount predicate, and a native nonzero
exit cannot expose the source exception class. SELECT/SHOW/DESC headers and rows,
affected writes, empty result behavior, and nonzero value-free failure behavior
are covered by direct, registry, CLI, source-derived, and differential mock tests.

At the R9.3p baseline, the E5.2 harness preserved all prior 65 ordered cases and
appended 20 production binary cases (85 exact cases, zero skips): scalar/table SELECTs with independent
native observations, a reserved disposable database DDL/DML lifecycle and native
postconditions, multiline/comment/quoted SQL, invalid database/auth/connection,
finite timeout, oversize input, and independent 1064 diagnostic classification.
The query live cases require an explicit workflow opt-in and use only runtime-
generated disposable credentials; repository/organization secrets and arbitrary
untrusted PR SQL are never used. Reports remain value-free and cleanup verifies
database removal. The SQLite job and prior pins are unchanged.

Evidence boundary:

* **Local mock/static evidence (executor `backend-engineer-senior`):** Podman
  gofmt, focused/race/vet/report checks, direct/registry/CLI/differential tests,

  protected GitHub E5.2 job must execute the exact current inventory with `cases_skipped: 0`,
  publish a fresh value-free report, independently observe native outcomes,

  `security-engineer-senior` are independent review gates for the artifact; no
